data.description: An axe designed for medieval warfare, the head secured to the haft with langets.  Though formidable, it's lighter than the sort you'd use for felling trees, and would make an inferior tool for that purpose.
A large street sign, its aluminum pole uprooted.  An unreasonably strong person might be able to wield it like a crude axe.
A large, two-handed wood axe.  It makes a good melee weapon, but is a bit slow to recover between swings.
A primitive axe made from a small wedge of copper affixed to a short haft.
A socketed bronze axe with a work-hardened edge, tightly bound to the shaft with cords.
A one-handed hatchet.  Makes a great melee weapon, and is useful both for chopping things and hammering them.
A broad piece of stone with an edge narrow enough to roughly chop wood.
A chunk of steel with one edge hammered down to something resembling a cutting edge.  It works passably well, but really can't compare to a proper axe.
A stone adze, a primitive tool for smoothing or scraping wood objects.
A stone with a narrow edge affixed to a stick.  It can chop wood, but requires much more effort than a modern axe.
A two-handed war club used in feudal Japan by samurai against armored opponents, it's made from hardwood studded with metal.
A sturdy wooden cudgel once essential to the great American pastime.
An aluminum version of the tapered club used to play baseball.  It's lighter, stronger, and hits harder than the wooden variety.
A baseball bat made of foam rubber with a plastic handle.  Light and easy to wield, but almost completely ineffective if your goal is to hurt someone.
A telescoping baton.  Right now, it's collapsed for easy storage.  Activate to expand.

use_action.msg: You snap open your baton.

data.description: A telescoping baton that's extended and ready to bust some heads.  Activate to collapse.

use_action.msg: You collapse your baton.

data.description: A short, easily concealed bludgeoning weapon consisting of a weight embedded at the end of a short leather shaft.  Formerly used by law enforcement, this weapon is meant to stun or knock out the subject, although head strikes have a high risk of causing a permanent, disabling brain injury or being fatal.
A solid wood training katana, exactingly crafted to mimic the weight and balance of the real thing.  Despite its lack of a sharp metal edge, it's still quite capable as a blunt weapon.
A standard bowling pin.  This could make a decent weapon, if it came to that.
A baseball bat wrapped with barbed wire, giving it a little extra oomph without compromising its durability.
A walking stick designed to lean on, whether for mobility assistance or puttin' on the ritz.
A sinister looking cane made of plastic.  It has a shiny red orb gripped by claws at the handle.

variants.description: A sinister looking cane made of plastic.  It has a shiny red orb gripped by claws at the handle.
A plastic cane designed to look like a wizard's staff.  They shall not pass!
A plastic cane festooned with ribbons and glitter.

data.description: An aluminum rod with a brace and padding designed to help support the body using the arm.  It could be combined with another like it, or used on its own.
A pair of aluminum rods with a brace and padding designed to help support the body using the arms.  These would make for an abysmal weapon, but they'd help you get around on a broken leg.
A wooden rod with a brace designed to help support the body using the arm.  It could be combined with another like it, or used on its own.
A pair of wooden rods with a brace designed to help support the body using the arms.  These would make for an abysmal weapon, but they'd help you get around on a broken leg.
A pair of rods, one wood and one aluminum, with braces designed to help support the body using the arms.  These would make for an abysmal weapon, but they'd help you get around on a broken leg.
A short steel baton employed by Japanese police in the 17th and 18th century.  A small hook forks from the weapon just above the hilt, intended to aid in snagging or disarming opponents.
Mankind's oldest weapon: a length of wood tapered slightly to maximize weight at the business end -- in other words, a club.  This one is quite short, prioritizing speed over power.
A short bit of wood with nails driven through the business end to create a menacing, if inelegant, weapon.
A thin aluminum rod with a heavy head on one end for hitting golf balls.  It looks quite fragile, but it could do a fair bit of damage before the shaft got too bent.
A heavy steel head on a long shaft, designed for demolition work.  It's a very hard-hitting melee weapon, but slow to swing and will probably exhaust you quickly.
A stout and hefty hammer, more akin to a mini sledge than a claw or ball-peen.  It's useful for portable demolition work, but unwieldy as a weapon.
A curved wooden stick with with a flat paddle at one end, commonly used by hockey players.
A flat wooden club with sharpened flakes of stone, ceramic, or glass stuck to both sides, a reasonable facsimile of the weapons once used by Aztec warriors.
A flat wooden club with impossibly-sharp teeth stuck to both sides, a postapocalyptic facsimile of the weapons once used by Aztec warriors.
A modern reimagining of the ancient Aztec weapon, made of a flat wooden club inset along its edges with steel razor blades.
A long wooden staff reinforced with steel langets and ferrules.

Halfway between a short spear and a long club, the goedendag consists of a heavy metal spike mounted to the end of an even heavier shaft.  It is unsophisticated, but was once a favorite among medieval infantry who needed a cheap, simple means to smash through enemy armor.
A medieval hammer with a spike on one end, made for battle.  Its odd shape and balance make it an excellent weapon, but an ineffective tool.
A versatile polearm with a spiked hammer head, a spike, and a hook attached to a beefy wooden pole.
A medieval weapon consisting of a wooden handle with a knob-shaped steel head.
data.//: Lighter and more accurate than the morning star.

A stick with a lump of bronze at one end.  While not as durable as steel, its heft makes it every bit as effective.

A large hammer, forged from the heart of a dying star.  It bears the inscription:

Whosoever holds this hammer,

CRUSH!'
A medieval weapon consisting of a wood handle with a spiked metal ball on the end.  It is bigger and heavier than a typical mace, and its spikes can deal serious damage to soft targets.
A baseball bat with several nails driven through it.  The spikes look dangerous, but they're sure to make it less durable.
A hefty plank of wood.  The nails driven through one end look nasty enough, but it remains a very awkward weapon.
A hardwood stick designed for hitting colorful balls around a felt table.  Truly, the coolest of sports.

data.description: A long, thin stick carved smooth for an easy grip.  These are commonly used by hikers to help navigate steep slopes, and could serve as a fighting staff, though this one looks too thin to last for long.
A fighting staff carved out of wood.  Lightweight and good for defense, it is surprisingly easy to handle.
A wooden staff weapon used in Okinawan martial arts.  It has been finely sanded and treated with oil for integrity.
A stout, knotty stick with a large knob at the top that is presently soaking in oil.  When it's done, it should be ready to bust some heads.

A stout, knotty stick with a large knob at the top that has been left to cure in a chimney.  A traditional Irish weapon, the shillelagh was originally used for settling disputes in a gentlemanly manner.

A stout knotty stick with a large knob at the top that has been left to cure in a chimney.  A traditional Irish weapon, the shillelagh was originally used for settling disputes in a gentlemanly manner.  The knob has been hollowed and filled with molten heavy metal to pack more of a punch.
A curved wooden club with a ball head carved from a root burl.  These devastating weapons were once used by indigenous peoples across North America.
A curved wooden club cradling a stone head.  It is currently soaking in oil and won't be properly fit for combat for a while longer.
A curved wooden club with a ball head carved from a root burl.  These weapons were once used by indigenous peoples across North America.
A curved wooden club cradling a stone head.  These weapons were once used by indigenous peoples across North America.

An ironshod quarterstaff that has a high-voltage stun gun built into the handle.  The stun gun is wired to the metal caps at either end of the staff, allowing you to zap a dangerous opponent should beating them senseless with it prove too hazardous.

A reinforced plastic tonfa; the core is filled with capacitors and a high-yield rechargeable storage battery.  When a switch on the handle is pressed, a high-voltage current is transmitted to the two electrodes mounted in the end of the tonfa, and by extension to anyone unfortunate enough to be in contact with them.  It also has a nifty flashlight, which is off at the moment.

A reinforced plastic tonfa; the core is filled with capacitors and a high-yield rechargeable storage battery.  When a switch on the handle is pressed, a high-voltage current is transmitted to the two electrodes mounted in the end of the weapon, and by extension to anyone unfortunate enough to be in contact with them.  The integral flashlight is turned on, continually draining power and lighting the surrounding area.
A hard plastic truncheon commonly employed by police.  Originally an Okinawan weapon, it consists of a stick with a perpendicular handle attached a third of the way down its length.
A stout wooden truncheon of the sort commonly employed by police.  Originally an Okinawan weapon, it consists of a stick with a perpendicular handle attached a third of the way down its length.
A foot-long blade made from high-tech alloy and edged with bonded nanocrystals.
A plank with a handle and a whittled-down point.  It's only a facsimile of a sword, but might serve for training or just knocking heads.
A plank with a handle and a whittled-down point, left large enough to require two hands.  It's only a facsimile of a sword, but might serve for training or just knocking heads.
A vicious single-edged sword made out of sheet metal layered twice over itself then welded together.  It's not as robust as a proper forged sword, but the edge is wickedly sharp.
A long-handled single-edged sword made out of sheet metal layered thrice over itself then welded together.  The extra length and weight makes it a tad awkward, but gives it a lot of slashing power.
A hand-forged approximation of a medieval weapon.  It's certainly sharp enough to get the job done, but the simplistic design is clearly inferior to the real thing.
A large, crudely-forged blade.  It's too big to be called a sword.  Too massive, too thick, too heavy, and far too rough.
data.//: CLANG

data.description: A large blade with one end wrapped in duct tape to make a crude handle, making it easier to wield as a rough machete.
This intimidating blade makes an excellent tool for chopping through vegetation, or anything else you don't want in your yard.
A thin, wobbly steel blade with sawteeth on one side and a flat chisel tip for digging.  More of a jackass of all trades than a jack of them.
A curved sword associated with cavalry from the Early Modern period onward.  Lightweight, but a deadly slashing weapon.

An ancient Chinese doubled-edged straight sword, with an ornate guard and a tassel attached to the pommel.  One of the four major weapons in folklore, alongside the dao sabre, qiang spear, and gun staff.
Also called a tuck, the estoc is a very long thrusting sword designed for piercing armor on the battlefield.

A classic medieval sword, in between the lighter arming sword and later two-handed swords in size.  It's well-balanced and surprisingly easy to use due to its two-handed grip, but requires a larger baldric or scabbard compared to smaller swords.
A classic medieval sword, just the right size to use one-handed.
A bronze sword of ancient Greek origin.

This ancient bronze weapon features a curved, sickle-like blade sharpened on the outside edge.  Associated with the New Kingdom period of Ancient Egypt, it was designed mainly to hack through the light armor common to the region.
An ancient Chinese saber consisting of a curved blade and a guard with a cupped design.  This one is made of bronze.
A simple short sword made of bronze.
A long, knife bladed bayonet that can be attached to the front of a rifle, converting it into a pike.  It is long enough to be used as a short sword when unmounted.
data.//: Based on the M1917 Bayonet.

data.description: An ornate knife that dates back to the Heian period in Japan.  Originally a backup weapon for samurai, these blades took on a ceremonial purpose, becoming the instrument used for seppuku.
A comparatively-common Japanese short sword.  Smaller and lighter than a katana, but still effective in combat.
A glass shard with wrapping at one end so it can be safely wielded.
A huge two-handed sword from Germany.  It packs a real wallop.
A two-handed sword from Japan resembling an extremely long katana.
A weapon used for fencing, the most noble of all sports.  Unfortunately, a fencing foil is rather useless as a weapon due to its flexible shaft and dull tip.

What was once a mostly-harmless fencing foil has had its electrical plunger assembly removed and has been crudely sharpened to a point.  Though it still lacks a cutting edge, it is now somewhat more lethal, yet still familiar to the practiced fencer.

The modifications made to this fencing foil may not be sporting, but they might give you an edge in this final competition.  Extra effort has been made to insulate the grip and a high voltage stun gun has been attached to the guard, wired through the electronic scoring circuit to the tip.  Thrusting the sharpened tip into a foe and activating the momentary switch will deliver a painful electric shock.

A weapon used for fencing, the most noble of all sports.  While not designed for combat the épée is the heaviest and stiffest of the fencing weapons, and therefore perhaps still useful in your situation.

What was once a mostly-harmless fencing épée has had its electrical plunger assembly removed and has been crudely sharpened to a point.  Though it still lacks a cutting edge, it is now considerably more lethal, yet still familiar to the practiced fencer.

The modifications made to this fencing épée may not be sporting, but they might give you an edge in this final competition.  Extra effort has been made to insulate the grip and a high voltage stun gun has been attached to the guard, wired through the electronic scoring circuit to the tip.  Thrusting the sharpened tip into a foe and activating the momentary switch will deliver a painful electric shock.
Unlike most cavalry sabers, the fencing saber is straight, and stouter than the foil or épée.  Designed for sport rather than real combat, it has a rounded tip and dull edges.

What was once a mostly-harmless fencing saber has had its rounded tip snapped off and has been crudely sharpened to a point.  Though it still lacks a cutting edge, it is now considerably more lethal, yet still familiar to the practiced fencer.

The modifications made to this fencing saber may not be sporting, but they might give you an edge in this final competition.  Extra effort has been made to insulate the grip and a high voltage stun gun has been attached to the guard, wired to the tip along the saber's groove.  Thrusting the sharpened tip into a foe and activating the momentary switch will deliver a painful electric shock.
A cane designed to conceal a blade.  This was a popular fashion accessory for the wealthy during the 18th and 19th centuries.
A sword with a thin blade designed to be hidden inside a hollow cane.
A straight sword that was ubiquitous during the Early Modern era, with a wide blade suitable for slashing or stabbing.  These were called "broad" to contrast with the slimmer rapiers of the day.
A thin, straight sword of the type once preferred by musketeers, masked gentlemen, and swashbucklers of all sorts.
A slightly curved sword from Japan, world-famous for its artistic design and association with the age of the samurai.
A Shaolin butterfly sword, short, with a handguard and an unusually wide blade.  These are traditionally used in pairs, but just one is more than enough.
A broad saber known for its use by sailors and pirates, as its short blade is easy to handle in close quarters.

A single-edged two-handed sword of German design, with a long, curved blade.  It became popular across Europe due to its low cost while maintaining strong cutting power in comparison to the more sophisticated longsword.
A distinct Dacian sword that curves forward, allowing you to bypass shields or hook and pull enemies, while delivering decent chopping damage.
A short, sharp double-edged dagger made to be gripped in the palm, with the blade protruding between the fingers.
Five pieces of rebar sharpened to cruel points and strapped to a brace fastened at the wrist and forearm on both arms.  The next bub better watch out.
This is a vintage spike bayonet for the British Lee Enfield No. 4 rifle, featuring a distinct cruciform blade and socket-based mounting system.
data.//: VERY not intended for usage unmounted.

data.description: An essential tool within any 20th-century Japanese soldier's toolbox, the Type 30 is a massive, single-edged sword-style bayonet intended for use with Arisaka rifles and even light machineguns.  Possessing a J-shaped quillon guard for hooking an opponent's weapon during combat, the bayonet, when dismounted, acts like a particularly sizable machete.
A curved sword used by the Raj of India in the 16th century, a talwar is usually impeccably decorated and able to take off a limb with a single swipe.

A Turkish sabre, the kilij is quite a bit heavier than most Middle Eastern sabres and has a distinctive wide tip called a yelman, which gives it vicious cutting power but means it requires a special scabbard.
generic item template
A sharp, heavy knife.  It makes a good melee weapon, and is an ideal item for butchering corpses.
A sharp knife designed for cutting meat.  It makes a poor melee weapon, but is decent at butchering corpses.
A short-bladed knife with a sharp blade, made for fine controlled cuts to vegetables without using a cutting board.

A long-bladed kitchen knife.  The blade is wider than the handle, giving room for the wielder's knuckles, and it has a characteristic curve for a fast rocking action for chopping vegetables.  It makes an acceptable melee weapon, but the wide blade is unwieldy for butchering.
A long-bladed kitchen knife with a thin, slightly curved blade for deftly slicing meat either in flat sheets or around the bone.  It makes a decent melee weapon, and is excellent for butchery.
This knife has quite a long blade with a scalloped edge for cutting bread.  It's not that sharp, but its length and heft mean it could do a bit of damage and cause some nasty tearing.
A menacing-looking knife with a broad, square shaped blade, curved for fast vegetable chopping.  Its heft and sharpness make it a decent weapon as well, although not as good as a meat cleaver.
A menacing-looking knife with a broad, square-shaped blade.  Its heft and sharpness would make it a very effective melee weapon and an excellent butchering tool.

A long, slim knife from the Renaissance era associated with knighthood, nobility, and warriors of Safavid Iran, these blades were as much a status symbol as an elegant tool for slipping through the gaps in metal armor.
A long, thin knife with a spring-loaded blade that rests inside the handle while not in use.
Also called a butterfy knife, this is a flashy knife with hinged handles that completely conceal the blade while folded.
A small folding knife with a locking blade and a pocket clip.  Not as good a weapon as a solid fixed-blade knife, but better than a penknife.
This large knife looks scary at first, but its hollow handle, the compass built into its pommel, and the saw teeth along the spine reveal that it's more of a novelty for wannabe survivalists.

pocket_data.description: A hidden handle compartment.  Unscrew the compass to access.

data.//: The swiss army knife is a bit more of a knife than a toolkit.
data.description: An iconic pocket knife imported from Europe.  Its red plastic handle conceals many small tools.

data.//: Highest non-powertool butchering quality.  It's made for skinning and butchering game, which is what you're generally doing.  Based on Buck 103 skinner.
data.description: Commonly used by hunters, this single-edged sheath knife is designed for cutting and skinning game rather than combat.

A modern bayonet in use with the US Marine Corps, adopted in an effort to improve USMC hand-to-hand fighting capabilities.  The bayonet is optimized to function as a fighting knife, sporting an ergonomic handle that will minimize hand fatigue during combat.  The blade tip is sharper in profile than other bayonets to assist in penetrating body armor, and also features a small serrated section to provide for some utility.
data.//: Modelled after the OKC3S bayonet.

data.description: The current issue Army bayonet, before the Cataclysm anyways.  It is thick, heavy, and surprisingly sharp.  This bayonet also functions as a wire cutter, and a mediocre saw for cutting through aircraft fuselage.  That the handle and tang can be completely disassembled from the blade is surely a fact of great comfort to the soldier, survivalist, and you.

A 6H4 bayonet for Kalashnikov pattern rifles, usually imported military surplus from eastern bloc countries.  The blade is made of stainless steel and the handle of a lightweight and durable plastic.  It features a middling metal saw on the spine of the blade, and can function as a wire cutter as well.  Though it is quite sturdy, it can't hold an edge very well.

data.//: An M9 Bayonet.

data.description: A Cold War era Army bayonet that has only partially been replaced by newer models.  It has an apocalypse-proof full-tang, double-edged high steel blade terminating in a spear point.  The no-frills design makes for both a good fighting knife and bayonet, a fact that was appreciated when reserve stocks of these were issued out to National Guardsmen.
data.//: An M4, M5, M6, or M7 Bayonet.

data.description: The KA-BAR was developed by the United States Marine Corps in 1942 by modifying hunting knife designs to be more soldier-proof.  The handle is made of stacked leather washers, and the blade is made of easy to sharpen high steel, making for a popular fighting, hunting and utility knife.  The blade is marked 'USMC'.

Arguably the most famous combat knife in military history, this blackened double-edged knife is made of drop-forged steel and knurled brass.  The balance of the knife is such that it can be tossed from one hand to the other instinctively, and the spear point allows for easy insertion into an unsuspecting foe's heart.  While this knife is great in a fight, it's not very good as a tool.  The ricasso declares this to be a 'Fairbairn-Sykes knife', with a National Stocking Number of '1095-99-963-2037'.
This stout combat knife features a steel guard to protect the user's knuckles.  The guard can also be used for striking or blocking.
A knife consisting of a long, somewhat sharpened spike and a tightly-wrapped rag as a handle.  Not as good as a real knife, but it'll do in a pinch.
A femur or other bone, about 20 cm long, which has been broken at one end and sharpened into a cutting tool.  Its jagged edge is wicked but fragile.
data.//: literally 75% of a bone.

data.description: A medieval dagger forged from rough iron.  It is not the sharpest tool in the shed, but it is certainly one of the largest.
This wavy-bladed dagger is from Southeast Asia.  The design of the blade causes it to make broad, painful wounds.
This versatile implement is a modern take on a traditional weapon that originated in Nepal.  Featuring a heavy blade with an inwardly-curved edge, it can be used as both a tool and a weapon.
An oblong plastic object with the far end ground down into a stabbing point.
A knife made of crudely-worked copper with a simple handle.  Primitive, but a step above stone-age.
A cast bronze knife with a full tang, with a handle wrapped in cord and leather, work-hardened and sharpened to a fine edge.

data.//: Too small to be effectively used for butchering, still not bad at it due to serrated edge.
data.description: A short, sturdy knife with a serrated edge for cutting lines and straps, and a blunt tip for prying.  Used primarily by divers, this knife has been fitted with cork to slow its descent if dropped underwater, so it takes up more space than usual.
A sharp, knife-like tool used for harvesting honey from beehives.  Makes a passable melee weapon.
A small pocket knife.  It isn't great for combat, but it's better than nothing.  It's sharp enough to butcher with.
A sharpened stone set into a hollowed handle.  Not nearly as usable as a proper knife, but it's better than nothing.
A small knife designed for opening boxes.  It could cause some damage, but it really should be used against inanimate objects.  It is too small to effectively butcher corpses with.
A rock with sharpened edges, produced by knapping.  Works as a crude cutting and butchering tool, if nothing else is available.
An okinawan weapon consisting of a slender spike with two hooked tines just above the hilt.
A traditional Indonesian knife.  The blade is very short, but its curved design is perfect for precision attacks.
A ceremonial dagger carried by Sikh men.  This one is sharp and could be an effective weapon.
A long, slightly curved and hooked steel blade on the end of a sturdy shaft, usually used for clearing brush.  Some people call it a kaiser blade.
A long, slightly curved and hooked bronze blade on the end of a sturdy shaft.  It could be used to thoroughly ruin something's day, or to cut branches and small trees.
An agricultural tool with a long wooden shaft and four spikes.  It's normally used to lift hay, but the tines could do some damage in a fight.
A simple wooden pole with one end sharpened to a point.
A stout pole with one end sharpened to a point.
A stout wooden pole with a fire-hardened point.
You've gone through the effort of making a proper spear shaft, but instead of attaching something sharp to the end you just whittled a point into the wood.  The peak of pointy stick technology.
This farming tool has been modified into an improvised weapon by rotating its blade 90 degrees, transforming it into a deadly giant blade on the end of a stick.  It's quite fragile, however.
A sturdy pole with a broad cutting blade securely bolted to one end.  It's intimidating despite being clearly homemade.
A stout wooden pole with the blade of a knife bolted into place at the end.  The shape of a knife blade isn't ideal for a spear, but it's still very sharp and effective.
A stout wooden pole with a sharp stone spearhead.
A long stick with a sharp stone spearhead.
A stout wooden pole with a spearhead worked from copper.
A spear with a bronze head.
A stout wooden pole with a hand-forged steel spearhead.
A shorter spear designed for use in close quarters.  Weapons like these were once used by fighting forces around the world, from the Vikings to the Zulu.
A shorter spear with a bronze head.  What it lacks in reach it more than makes up for in maneuverability.
Also known as a fire iron, this short rod has a pointed tip with a hook on one side.  It was designed for stoking firewood, but it looks like it could really do some damage in a fight.
A pipe with one end cut off at an angle.

data.//: Better balanced and more accurate, but less base damage than a steel spear.
data.description: A Chinese spear in use since antiquity. The tip is larger than most european spears, and there's typically a decorative tassel hung just below it.
A versatile polearm with an axe blade, a spike, and a hooking beak attached to a long, sturdy haft.
A sturdy polearm with a sizable single-edged blade on the end.

A lightweight Japanese polearm reminiscent of a sharply curved katana with an exceptionally long handle.  Originally a battlefield tool, they eventually came to be used for home defense, and were widely used for this purpose by women of the samurai class.
A fire-hardened wooden spear honed to a sharper point.
A steel-tipped wooden throwing spear.
A medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft with a fire-hardened point.
A medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft tipped with a copper spearhead.
A medieval weapon consisting of a very long wooden shaft tipped with a steel spearhead.
A pole weapon with a curving single-edged blade.  Its blade bears some superficial resemblance to that of an agricultural scythe from which it likely evolved.
A polearm with an axe head, a small hammer on the back, and a short dagger-like spike on top.  It's surprisingly lightweight for its size, and specialized for cracking open heavy armor.
A bronze polearm that originated in the Shang dynasty of China, if not earlier.  It combines a long spear head with a perpendicular axe plade shaped like a crescent moon.
A leather hand and arm wrap incorporating metal plates over the knuckles to improve punching power and defense.
Also called tiger claws, these Indian weapons consist of two sets of finger rings that secure curved steel claws to the wearer's palms, allowing for vicious unarmed attacks while worn.
Two sets of metal rings connected to lugs which are worn over the fingers to add a good deal of power to the user's punches.
A pair of knuckles consisting of two small squares of wood with several nails sticking through them.  Useful in nasty street fights.
A mass of scrap metal crudely beat into shape, with folded rags underneath to protect the wearer's knuckles.
A pair of knuckles forged from steel, designed to be worn over the fingers to cause punches to do more damage.
A pair of gloves with studded metal knuckles and a thin back plating.
A pair of thick steel plates to wear over the knuckles.
A pair of metal braces, each with a single sturdy spike attached.  When strapped to your hands, the spikes protrude 5 centimeters past your clenched fists.

A very long strip of braided leather with a handle on one end.  Originally developed to settle disagreements with cattle, it's better used now for flaying the rotten flesh off of walking corpses.  Great for when a problem comes along.
data.//: Most whips are OK in melee, but bullwhips really need a lot of room to get going.

data.description: The "cat 'o nine tails", a handle with nine short leather whips, each sporting a razor-sharp metal tip.  This ancient instrument of torture can cause bleeding, but by design is inefficient as a weapon.
data.//: There's no way you can swing this thing without hitting SOMETHING.

data.description: A sharp metal spike tied to the end of a long rope, used primarily in Chinese martial arts.  Though often used for show, there's little doubt that a skilled fighter could do real damage with this thing.
A pair of nested socks with a stone tied inside.  A true weapon of desperation.
A stout pole with a spiked mace head attached to the end with a chain, a purpose-made combat version of the peasant flail.  It specializes in threshing people in metal armor, rather than grain.
A short pole with a spiked steel ball attached to it by a chain.
A stout pole with a wooden club attached to the end with a leather cord.  This farming tool was historically used to thresh grain, but was frequently pressed into service as a weapon.
A weapon originating from East Asia consisting of a pair of short sticks connected by a shorter rope or chain.  The design is a bit unwieldy, but fast and deadly in the right hands.
A long spool of chain with a steel weight at one end.  What a terrible night it'll be for anyone who gets hit by this thing.
A thin ribbon of flexible steel attached to a handle, the whip sword is an Indian weapon long renowned for its bizarre design and the skill required to properly use it.
A steel hook attached to a long rope.  Deploying this next to a wall might give you a way to climb up.
A rod ending in a leather popper originally used to stimulate a horse and give them orders.

Welcome to your Emergency Survival Shelter.  We hope your stay here will be short and comfortable.  Provided are an emergency blanket, high-visibility jacket, gas mask, and food and water rations for one day, as well as an emergency lighter and flashlight.  There are further supplies in the communal cabinets should the facility be over its intended capacity.  These resources are checked and updated by FEMA on a regular basis, but if you find some items missing, please contact a FEMA supervisor at your earliest convenience.

Please wait in the shelter until an official evacuation transport arrives to take you to your homes or, in the event of a major disaster, to the nearest evacuation gathering point.

In the event that you have been evacuated under violent circumstances, FEMA recommends taking cover in the shelter's basement until help arrives.  Remember: if you leave the shelter, we cannot find you to take you to safety.

A handmade poster notifying passersby about someone's missing cat, and requesting that anyone with information contact the listed phone number.
Posters promoting movies that were in theaters when the Cataclysm hit.

name.str: Last Stand 2: Still Standing movie poster

description.str: This a poster for the highly anticipated sequel "Last Stand 2: Still Standing".  Ashton Murphy reprises his role as Det. Harvey Baxter, a retired private eye who delivers pain to those who flee from justice.

variants.description: A poster promoting the animated movie "The Black Freighter", an adaptation of the novel of the same name.  The print is in the same style as the source material.
A white movie poster displaying a balding man in a stained hoodie waving lackadaisically.  He appears to be the title character.

name.str: Fyreguard: A Tale as Old as Time movie poster

variants.description: A vibrant poster displaying an astonishing landscape full of magical creatures.  Above the illustration is the title of the movie in a medieval font.
A poster for "Hunted III", the third entry of the "Hunted" slasher franchise.  Its tagline reads: "You can't outrun it forever".
A poster for "Cybercop 3D", a sci-fi movie about a policeman tasked to take down a group of dangerous hackers inside a simulated reality.

data.description: A small picture of something or somebody important to the owner, designed to be safely tucked into a wallet.
A weak bow crudely crafted from a single uncured wood stave.  It could be useful for hunting small game, or maybe even fish.
data.//: 30 lb draw weight, 52in, 20in draw, 0.259 slugs of momentum with a 30g arrow.

data.description: Emphasizing portability and agility over power, this all-wood bow is suitable for small game and harassing enemies.
data.//: 52in Elm Shortbow at 24in draw with 26in, 0.077 lb aspen arrow: 45J, 50 lbs draw, 0.35 slugs with 30g arrow.

data.description: A modern bow with shaped cams and extra cables for high-velocity shots that can be used effectively by fairly strong archers.  Currently set to a medium weight.
data.//: 70 lb draw weight 24in draw, 100J, 0.55 slugs of momentum with a 30g arrow.

use_action.msg: You tighten the limbs, increasing the strength of the bow.

data.description: A modern bow with shaped cams and extra cables for high-velocity shots that can be used effectively by very strong archers.  Currently set to a high weight, and ready to cause some real damage - if you can draw it.
data.//: 80 lb draw weight, efficient, 0.62 slugs of momentum with a 30g arrow.

use_action.msg: You loosen the limbs, decreasing the strength of the bow.

data.description: A modern bow with shaped cams and extra cables for high-velocity shots that can be used effectively by average archers.  Currently set to a low weight, making it much easier to draw.
data.//: 40 lb draw weight, efficient, 0.45 slugs of momentum with a 30g arrow.

use_action.msg: You tighten the limbs, increasing the strength of the bow.

data.description: A heavily recurved short bow made of wood, bone, and horn laminated together.  Its shape and construction give it a formidable draw weight despite its size.
data.//: 100 lb draw weight, 28in draw, 110J, 0.598 slugs of momentum with a 32g arrow.

data.description: The fiberglass limbs of this modern-day short bow curve back on themselves, giving it a decent amount of power despite its size.  It can be activated to fold down for easy storage when not in use.
data.//: 52in Fiberglass recurved bow at 26in draw, 80lb draw, 82J, 0.51 slugs with 30g arrow.

use_action.msg: You disassemble your bow.

data.description: A modern fiberglass bow that has been taken down for storage.  Activate it to assemble it for use.
data.//2: When taken down.

use_action.msg: You assemble your bow.

data.description: A wooden longbow nearly the height of a man.  Though it resembles a medieval weapon of war, the modest draw weight means this weapon is more suited for shooting targets or animals than penetrating chain mail.
data.//: 70in Yew Longbow at 28in, 65 lbs draw, 60J, 0.41 slugs with 30g arrow

data.description: A long bow as tall as a man, this is a convincing reproduction of the weapons that ruled the battlefield prior to the invention of gunpowder.  The incredible draw weight is too much for the average person, but in the right hands it could be devastating.
data.//: 78in Yew Longbow at 30in draw with 31in, 145 lbs draw, 0.51 slugs with 30g arrow.

data.description: An extremely large, powerful compound bow, made with enormous limbs and a thick string to take an immense amount of energy.  A pulley system makes it a bit easier to draw, though it would still be quite a feat of strength for any human.
data.//: 150 lb draw weight, very efficient, 0.5 slugs of momentum with a 30g arrow.

data.description: Although spear throwing contraptions were used throughout the entire world, this design in particular hails from Mesoamericas.  It was especially popular among Peruvian natives, despite the Nahuatl origin of the name.  It is essentially a carved piece of wooden shaft with a hollowed space to place the projectile of the same name.  It'll also do well as a melee weapon in a pinch.
data.//2: Significantly worse accuracy than a bow. See 'Comparing Atlatls and Bows: Accuracy and Learning Curve' by John C Whittaker

data.description: A smaller, mounted version of the Greco-Roman ballista, for those situations where the crossbow just isn't enough.  Unlike crossbows, it is powered by a torsion spring that is wound by a hand crank and uses two prods instead of one bow.  Its size and design make it unfeasible to be used by hand, requiring it to be set down or mounted to a vehicle.
data.//0: Effective range significantly limited by arc of shot and complete lack of optics. 1 range = 12m gives us about 300m of range, which is a decent bit even for a skilled Roman artilleryman, firing at a formation or large structure.
data.//1: Slightly worse than a composite bow, errors in hand-manufacturing build up as the overall product gets larger.
data.//2: Shooter's view is badly offset from the angle of launch. Even in a best case scenario (straight shooting, no drop), there is no dedicated sighting device.
data.//3: Aiming is solely dependent on the user's grip, which must be removed to handle reloading. This weapon must be completely re-aimed with every use.

data.description: A big steel tipped projectile, twice the size of a normal bolt and much heavier than one.  It gets thicker towards the base, and is fletched there with the protrusions of the shaft itself.
data.//1: Slightly worse than a broadhead arrow, errors in hand-manufacturing build up as the overall product gets larger.
data.//2: With the amount of kinetic energy these things have, reusing them is quite unlikely.

data.description: Also called a stonebow, this light crossbow fires pebbles or other small projectiles rather than bolts with surprising accuracy, if not a lot of power.

A modern reverse-draw crossbow engineered to be compact and quiet without sacrificing firepower.  Despite its diminutive size, this weapon ought to be sufficient for taking deer, or perhaps even larger targets.
data.//: 27in Fiberglass pistol crossbow at 11in draw, 48J, 80 lbs draw, 0.3 Slugs with 30g bolt.

data.description: A small crossbow designed for use with one hand.  Due to its small size and simple construction, it is quite weak.
A crossbow made entirely of wood, save for the bowstring.  It simple design makes it easy to operate, but it's lacking in power.
data.//2: 150lb @ 10in powerstroke, 34in wood limbs, 37.7J, 0.337 slugs with a 0.066lb bolt
data.//volume: L 86 * W 25 * H 6 cm, volume is calculated as area of triangle multiplied by height

data.description: A lever lies in a recess carved into this crossbow's wooden stock, allowing it to be mechanically reloaded simply by lifting it out to catch the string and pressing it back into place.  This allows for rapid reloading despite the relatively heavy steel limbs.
data.//volume: L 86 * W 25 * H 6 cm, volume is calculated as area of triangle multiplied by height

data.description: A modern hunting crossbow with shaped cams and extra cables for high-power shots.  An integrated cocking rope assists the user with string pulling.
A medieval heavy crossbow designed to penetrate armor.  Its steel limbs can store a tremendous amount of energy, but it takes a lot of time and effort to load.

A lightweight wooden crossbow which can mount a magazine atop it, allowing for automatic fire via the operation of a lever which in a single motion spans the bow, nocks the bolt, and releases the string.
A modern hunting crossbow with shaped cams and extra cables for high-powered shots.  It is mounted with a ten-bolt magazine and a pump-action lever for rapid reloads.
A slender medieval crossbow with four steel limbs and two bowstrings.  With the aid of a foot stirrup, it may be loaded with two bolts and fired twice in succession.

The Portable Plasma Accelerator Model Five, as its digital display proudly calls it, is a prototype weapon which uses a pulsed laser to give the air between itself and its target an electrical charge, then uses that brief moment of conductivity to deliver a payload of ionized gas that explodes in a brilliant and incredibly hot display on impact.  It's a bit like if a rocket launcher fired lightning bolts made out of that blue fire that you see when you microwave things you're not supposed to.

A prototype weapon which uses a pulsed laser to charge the air between itself and the target, then delivers a packet of ionized gas along the resulting current, which explodes on impact to set targets alight and play havoc with electronics.
A disposable light anti-tank rocket launcher.  Once fired, it cannot be reloaded and must be disposed of.
data.//: A tube with a lever.  Unsurprisingly, dirt cheap (at least for a rocket launcher).

data.description: The emblematic RPG-7 launcher.  Its simple, inexpensive, and reliable design made it a popular choice among armies and insurgent groups worldwide.
data.//: Like the LAW, this thing is basically a tube with a lever.  It's even cheaper in terms of construction, but there's a premium due to being imported.  Also not disposable.

data.description: A water cannon from a fire truck.  Mounted on a vehicle, it could be used to stop fires or "protesters".
An air gun modeled to look like a small lever-action rifle.  Designed for young shooters and low-risk target practice, it's fairly accurate, but the BBs it fires deal nearly no damage.
data.//: You could get a Red Ryder at walmart for $32, but you'd shoot your eye out x_-

data.description: A cheap varmint air rifle chambered in .177, suitable for hunting small game.
data.//: Based on the Gamo Varmint .177, with 1200fps PBA/1000fps Lead

data.description: Little more than a strip of leather, the sling is an ancient weapon that acts as an extension of the wielder's arm, allowing small stones and custom-made bullets to be fired much faster and farther than they could be thrown by hand.

A children's toy consisting of a Y-shaped piece of wood with an elastic band between the arms.  It can be used fire gravel or other very small projectiles with surprising speed.  It's probably not fit for killing zombies, but might be useful for hunting smaller game.
Also called a fustibalus, this is a wooden staff with a sling fastened to one end.  When swung, it acts like a trebuchet to hurl rocks much farther and faster than throwing them by hand.
data.//: The staff sling,consists of a staff with a short sling at one end.

data.description: A modern slingshot with a wrist brace, allowing it to fire tiny objects slightly more forcefully than a simple wooden slingshot.

A sophisticated underwater fishing implement designed to fire a specialized type of spear, with a dedicated hand pump to use with it.  While highly effective when used underwater, it is nearly useless on dry land.
data.//: https://www.mares.com/en_US/injector-for-pneumatic-guns + https://www.mares.com/en_US/cyrano-1-1-8
data.//2: 1340g for a gun + 790g for pump

data.description: Underwater fishing device, this speargun has set of two rubber bands.  It doesn't make you able to load two spears, but it can put a bit more power into shot.  While highly effective when used underwater, it is nearly useless on dry land.
data.//: https://amz.run/7XJA

data.description: A long underwater fishing implement designed to fire a specialized type of spear using tension in a rubber band.  While highly effective when used underwater, it is nearly useless on dry land.
data.//: https://amz.run/7XJ4

data.description: An underwater fishing implement designed to fire a specialized type of spear using tension in a rubber band.  While highly effective when used underwater, it is nearly useless on dry land.

data.description: A rope with stone weights at either end.  If thrown, these might trip a person or animal, provided it isn't too small or too big.
A plastic disc made for playing disc golf.  It is smaller and denser than a normal frisbee.
A plastic frisbee made for outdoor games.
A mesh of weights and cordage designed to entangle opponents in combat.  It probably won't work on anything too small or too big.
A large plastic dart made for outdoor games.
A fletched wooden dart with a steel tip backed up by a lead weight.  Darts like these were a mainstay in the armies of ancient Rome.
An all-steel handaxe made specially for throwing.  With cutouts along the haft to reduce weight and an unevenly S-curved blade, it makes a poor tool and a questionable melee weapon.
A thin, flat knife made for throwing.  Its ineffective cutting edge and odd shape make it unsuitable for use as a tool.
A stick carved into a shape suitable for throwing at a target.  It's not a boomerang, so don't expect it to return to your hand.
A ring-shaped throwing blade, sharpened all along its outer edge.  The unconventional design can deliver exceptional cutting force thanks to the spin the thrower imparts to the weapon.
Some kind of prototypical electronic device with exposed wiring.  Some of the wires have bare ends that could be connected together.
A vintage, bright-red Bakelite phone of famous Swedish design.  It would look almost normal, if not for the fact that its rotary dial has been replaced with a doorknob.
A small, delicate golden comb.  It was once carefully engraved, but time has smoothed its designs to illegibility.
A smooth ring of steel, heavy under the weight of numerous keys.  The designs of the keys change over time, but none will fit any keyhole you have ever found.
A small cube of smooth rock.  A uniform grid of nine squares is engraved in each of its faces.
A squat teapot with a minimalist design.  Its surface shines under the glow of unseen light sources.
A small digital stopwatch, looking slightly old by today's standards.  Its digital display prints ever-changing gibberish.
A slightly worn button-down shirt with a tropical pattern, straight out of the 80's.  You swear that every time you look away and look back, the pattern changes subtly.
A strange golden badge in the shape of a shield with scratched out lettering.  The faceless figures decorating the badge seem taller and thinner than ordinary humans.
A pair of thin, round sunglasses.  The tinted glass seems to reflect the same shade of baleful orange light no matter what light it reflects.
A pair of ornately decorated steel scissors.  The handle is decorated with vicious-looking birds.
A heart-shaped silver locket with an black-and-white image of a smiling woman in it.  Her eyes seem to follow you whenever you look at it.
A jacket traditionally worn by school athletes.  The logo of the school has an oddly detailed fractal pattern that draws your eye in whenever you look at it.
A long apron with a plain pattern on it.  Your eyes can't seem to decide what color it is.
A thin, palm-sized disc of incredibly dense stone, engraved with meaningless swirls.  Its surface seems to repel grime and debris, and it refuses to tarnish or scratch.
This brick of too-dense stone is warped in a way that just barely makes it worthless as a building material.  Its smooth surface is unmarred by texture, dirt, or color.
A shattered fragment of alien resin.  It looks a bit like a large piece of sea glass, frosted and gritty with the edges rounded off.  It is somewhat warm to the touch.

A large pod the size of a beer keg, filled with gooey alien resin.  Squeezing it firmly causes resin to squirt from the broken stalk at the end, hardening within a few seconds of being exposed to the air.

A branching trunk of leaves from a massive fern, about two feet long and a couple of feet across in diameter when including the leaves.  Maybe one day you'll think of something to make with a giant fern.
A collection of hand-soldered wires leading to plugs and what looks like a micro controller.  The plugs look like they could be attached to you, assuming you have a Standard Neurobionic Interface.
A collection of mismatched pipes, wires, and a central device that looks like a micro controller.  It almost looks like it could be used for some form of central cooling.
Thin metallic strips with an ochre sheen, interlaid together into a flexible mesh.  You can't tell whether it's a circuit, a heat dissipation component, or a mechanical actuator.
A slightly curved plate of white metal.  It readily collects low amounts of static charge.
A collection of tiny metal strips, spheres, and other geometric primitives taken from a disassembled alien machine.
A very heavy sphere, presumably made almost entirely of gold.  The complex pattern etched across its surface implies that it might serve some exotic function.
A robotic assembly of unknown function.  Entirely made from tight-fitting metal plates, it somewhat resembles the interior of a mechanical clock.
A carved sphere embedded with small black glass screens.  It's probably a sensor of some kind.
The dismantled stovetop of an electric oven.  Some electric components are still attached, but the heating elements have been pulled off.
A large, hefty steel box that was once the main body of an electric oven.  Most of the parts have been stripped.  It could be further disassembled into base materials.
The control panel and LCD from a dismantled electric oven.
The removed glass and steel door of an electric oven.
A simple sheet metal drawer that goes in the bottom of an electric oven.
A bone from some creature or other.  Could be used in cooking and crafting.
data.//: Values based roughly on a male human femur.

data.description: A bone from some unfortunate creature.  It doesn't look human.
A tremendous bone taken from some gigantic creature.
data.//1: Values based roughly on an adult female African elephant femur. 61 times the size of the normal bone.
data.//2: While it would make sense to be able to mill it, the bone won't fit into a mill…

data.description: Gray-brown cracks and gouges mar this bone like decay in an old tooth.
data.//: Not for use in edible recipes, and should require ~200% as much as normal for applicable inedible recipes except for charcoal.

data.description: A bone from a human being.  It could be used to make some stuff, if you're feeling sufficiently ghoulish.
data.//: No extend support for vitamins, we need to overwrite

data.description: An off-white powder made from grinding bones.
This is a grayish bone meal made from rotten bones.  It's probably not safe to use for anything edible.
A thin skewer carved from bone.  Sadly, it won't make squirrel on a stick taste better.
This is a dummy item.  If you see it something went wrong.
The skull of a human being.  Carrying this around probably isn't going to win you any friends.
The stained skull of what was once a human being.  It is rotted and noticeably warped from its lively form.  Carrying this around probably isn't going to win you any friends.
The skull of a tiny canine, likely a Chihuahua or another similarly sized dog breed.
The skull of a small canine, likely a small dog breed.
The skull of a wolf or a dog.  Essential material for building an articulated wolf skeleton.
The skull of a what looks like a dog, although it has an extra eye socket.
The skull of a small feline, likely a house cat.
The skull of a medium-sized feline, likely a bobcat.
The skull of a tiger.
The skull of a raccoon.
The skull of a bear.
The skull of an opossum.
The skull of a skunk.
The skull of a small rodent, most likely a rat.
The skull of a rabbit or a hare.
The skull of a beaver.
The skull of a pig, either a domestic or a wild one.
The skull of a domestic sheep.
The skull of a goat with the horns still attached.
The skull of a bovine, likely a domestic cow, with the horns still attached.
The skull of a horse.  Given the circumstances you can be pretty sure it was a domestic horse.
The skull of a cervine, either a deer or a reindeer.
The skull of a cervine, probably a deer…  But why does it have eight eye sockets?
The skull of a moose.
The skull of a moose, sporting big curving tusks, like a boar.
The skull of a llama.

A handful of small, water-soluble white crystals with a watery metallic odor, historically used for many different purposes.  Also known as potash alum and potassium aluminum sulfate; often called simply alum, as it's the most important member of the generic class of compounds called alums.
A handful of powdered colorful cloth dye, which can be used to dye many fabrics if combined with water and some mordant.
A handful of white, odorless, strongly hygroscopic powder with an extremely salty taste.  Often used as a de-icing agent or as dessicant.
A handful of white, odorless, hygroscopic powder, also known as soda ash or washing soda.  Despite the name, it isn't used for cleaning, though it is one ingredient of detergent.

Also known as sodium bicarbonate, this is a white, odorless powder with a slightly salty alkaline taste.  It's often used in baking as a leavening agent, but can be put toward a wide variety of other purposes.
Elemental mercury, unique in that it is a liquid under normal temperatures and pressures.  Known for its use in thermometers.

A handful of gray powder that is highly sensitive to friction, heat, and shock.  Often used as a primary explosive, and historically in percussion caps and primers for self-contained firearm ammunition.
data.//: density: 4.42 g/cm3

data.description: A chunk of sodium, a highly reactive soft gray metal, immersed in anhydrous mineral oil to prevent it from oxidizing in the air during storage.
A chunk of potassium, a highly reactive soft gray metal, immersed in anhydrous mineral oil to prevent it from oxidizing in the air during storage.
A handful of white powder that is used in detonators to detonate secondary explosives.  It replaced mercury fulminate in modern ammunition primers.

data.description: A large sheet of leather.  You could use it as a picnic blanket, but it's more valuable as a surface for butchering as it does not soak up blood.  It's rolled and ready for carrying.

A large mat woven from fibrous material.  You could use it as a picnic blanket, but it's more valuable as a surface for butchering.  Too thin to be used as a comfortable sleeping mat.  It's rolled and ready for carrying.
A large wooden container used to turn raw milk into butter and buttermilk.  This model uses a foot crank and holds three gallons of raw milk.
A small water-powered mill that can convert starchy products into flour.  Needs to be placed via the construction menu.
A small wind-powered mill that can convert starchy products into flour.  Needs to be placed via the construction menu.
A large screw press for manually pressing oil out of fruit or seed paste.  Needs to be placed via the construction menu.
A massive bench-mounted device with a short guillotine blade mounted to a long lever.  Designed for making straight or curved cuts through sheet metal up to 3 millimeters thick.

data.description: A point-and-shoot digital camera with a digital viewfinder, a backup 'iron-sight', and flash.  You can look at your photos on the digital screen, or transfer them with any standard electronic device.

data.description: A 35 mm digital SLR (single-lens reflex) camera with optical and digital viewfinders, a zoom lens with auto-focus and stabilizer, and flash.  You can look at your photos on the digital screen or transfer them with any standard electronic device.  Before the Cataclysm, you could have taken professional-grade photos using this.
data.//: swappable, but proprietary 160g Li-Ion battery

data.description: A cellphone, an older cousin of the smartphone that is still popular in certain circles due to its reliability and sturdiness.  Using the phone will turn it on and provide light, assuming it is sufficiently charged.  It also tells the time and has an alarm feature.

data.description: An antenna designed to pick up signals better when pointed at the source.  You could use this with a radio to receive faint signals.

A pair of electronic handcuffs, used by police and riot bots to detain captives.  Their continuous siren clearly identifies the wearer as an arrested criminal and alerts human police.  Wait for their arrival, don't try to escape or to remove the cuffs - they will administer an electric shock.
However, since the only police likely to respond are undead, you may have a long wait ahead, unless you get creative…

data.description: A tool for measuring radiation.  Using it will prompt you to choose whether to scan yourself or the terrain, or to turn on continuous scan, which will provide continuous feedback on ambient radiation.  It is currently off.

data.description: A tool for measuring radiation.  It is in continuous scan mode, and will produce quiet clicking sounds in the presence of ambient radiation.  Using it allows you to turn it off, or scan yourself or the ground.

data.description: This strange contraption appears to be little more than a laminated box built around a battery, a poorly backlit screen, and a wound spool of cloth netting.  The letters "X E D R A" are emblazoned on the side.  To operate the device, unfurl the netting and place it around the object to analyze.  Despite not appearing to do anything, it consumes an enormous amount of electricity and provides a brief numerical readout.
data.//: Battery only, intentionally. Meant for field expeditions to other dimensions where grid power is unavailable. Too advanced for the player to make grid-useable.

data.description: A strange apparatus, seemingly consisting of a glass-encased microphone linked to a small thermal printer and digital screen.  The screen remains perpetually blank, save for a battery indicator on its upper right, and on its left side lies a single red button: "PRINT DATA".

use_action.description: Activate the recorder's printer

data.description: A hand-powered battery charger.  It has an adjustable receptacle designed to accept a wide variety of rechargeable battery cells.

A portable computer, ubiquitous tool both before and after the cataclysm.  While it is little you can do with it nowadays, mostly from lack of internet, you still can load it with books (or even scan using frontal camera)

data.description: A ubiquitous communication device that once connected users to the internet via a worldwide cellular network, now reduced to a mere computer.  Capable of taking photos with its integrated camera and illuminating an area with its flashlight app, assuming it has enough charge.  The smartphone also has a clock app that includes an alarm and an app for tracking consumed calories.  Runs on a small, rechargeable power cell compatible with a Unified Power Supply.

data.description: A portable power supply housed in a sleek black box.  A cable on one end allows it to charge from a power grid while ports at the other sit ready to feed power to any compatible devices.
A direct methanol fuel cell which can provide electricity to devices compatible with a standard power bank by oxidizing methanol supplied from a specialized fuel tank to produce electricity.
This battery-devouring device is just the thing to knead the tension out and help you relax.  Use it to take a break and unwind.
A long prying tool with a slender wedge at either end.  Use it to open locked doors without destroying them, or to lift manhole covers.

A pair of thin pieces of metal, one bent in an 'L' shape to push tumblers and the other acting as a torsion wrench.  These tools are almost totally inadequate for picking locks, but when you've got nothing else, it might work.
An improvised pick and torsion wrench made from scrap metal.  You'll need MacGyver-like skills to open locks with these as they are brittle, but they lower the chances of alarms being set off.
A short ice axe with a spiked head and a small hammer on the other end, a multi-purpose hiking and climbing tool used by mountaineers.  It is sturdy enough to lift manhole covers.
A pipe with both ends bent and hammered flat to resemble a crowbar.  It's a poor weapon and a terrible prying tool, but sometimes you have to make do.
A locksmith's set of sturdy steel lockpicks and torsion wrenches.  It is essential for silently and quickly opening locks, provided you have some lockpicking and mechanical skills.
this a pseudo item
A fragile container filled with acid.  Throw it to spill out a pool of potent acid.  It could also be used in a staff sling with a modified cradle.
A block of military-grade RDX composition explosive.  A label reads: "Highly explosive, use with extreme caution!" It comes with a small timer.
A block of military-grade RDX composition explosive.  A label reads: "Highly explosive, use with extreme caution!" It comes with a small timer, which is currently ticking down.
A stick of nitroglycerin and filler wrapped in waxed paper with a fuse coming out of one end.  It almost looks cartoonish, despite being a dangerous and barely-stable explosive.

This substantial device is a bomb that generates an electromagnetic pulse.  When activated, the plutonium fuel cell is drained into a flux compression generator, the detonation of which, in addition to the usual shrapnel and concussive force, creates a strong magnetic field.  When this magnetic field is fed into the antenna, it creates an electro-magnetic pulse which can permanently damage electronics and drain bionic energy.

data.description: The B54 Special Atomic Demolition Munition is an extremely powerful weapon, a portable nuclear bomb, using the smallest nuclear warhead in US inventory.  It is housed inside a extremely sturdy transit container.  Use it to activate the timer.  You guess that the explosion would be large enough to take out a small house.
The nuclear bomb looks no different from the outside, yet you know that the device is armed and counting down.  You should probably get far, far away from it.

A bottle of flammable liquid with a rag inserted.  Use this item to light the rag.  You will, of course, need a lighter or matches in your inventory to do this.  After lighting it, throw it to cause fires.

data.description: A bottle of flammable liquid with a flaming rag stoppered in its neck.  Throwing it will shatter the bottle on impact and ignite a fireball.  Dropping it will set you on fire, so don't do that unless you want to burn to death.
A device which, three seconds after being armed, will emit a short burst of microwave and radio interference which can briefly "stun" drones and other machines by overloading their electronics.

A plastic ring housing a propellant charge to help a mortar shell fly farther.  It's been detached from its cartridge and is now otherwise useless, but could be salvaged for the explosive material within.
A crudely-made electric firestarter, which can function as an inefficient lighter.

A simple item for starting fires with friction between a notched plank and wooden shaft.  The shaft is spun rapidly with a sawing motion by a bowstring wrapped around it.  Very slow to acquire a usable ember.

A simple item for starting fires by friction between a notched plank and wooden shaft, with a flywheel attached.  The shaft is spun rapidly with a pumping motion by a cord wrapped around it.  Slow to acquire a usable ember.
A piece of flint paired with a hardened high carbon steel striker.  Use it to spark a flame.

A disposable plastic lighter, capable of creating a small flame with the flick of a finger.  Allows you to use various drugs like cigarettes, light explosives like Molotov cocktails, or light nearby items on fire.
A magnifying glass, for closely examining fine details.  It can also be used for starting fires if direct sunlight is available.
A very low-quality focusing lens, made from non-optical-grade glass.  Useless for building most optical devices, but you can start a fire with it if sunlight is available.

A firestarting tool of Southeast Asian origin, consisting of a thin, hollow wooden cylinder sealed at one end and open at the other, and a wooden piston forming an airtight circular seal with it, making use of rapid and adiabatic air compression to ignite a piece of tinder.  It also comes with a tinder container to keep tinder dry.  Use it to start a fire.

A small book of matches with a coarse strike surface on the outside flap for lighting them. Due to the matches being lightly glued to the matchbook, they can be removed, but not replaced on the book.
A solid strike anywhere match.  One and done.

A small box of matches with a coarse strike surface on the side for lighting them.  Allows you to use various drugs like cigarettes, light explosives like Molotov cocktails, or light nearby items on fire.

A stylish lighter featuring a flip-top cover and a refuelable tank, capable of creating a small flame with the flick of a finger.  Allows you to use various drugs like cigarettes, light explosives like Molotov cocktails, or light nearby items on fire.

A fire extinguisher in grenade form.  While not as effective as a regular fire extinguisher, you can use it from a farther distance.  It has a plastic plug that can be pulled, but is primarily activated by heat, so just throw it into the flames.

data.description: An active extinguisher grenade, likely to burst any second now.  Better throw it!
A durable tool consisting of a sturdy fiberglass shaft tipped with a small steel hook.
data.//: If the pole itself has a diameter of around 3 cm which is thick, to be frank, then we half it for the radius -> 1,5 cm, square it -> 2,25, mulitplicate with pi -> ~7,07 cm² multiplicate with 160 cm length -> 1130 cm³ which is 1,13 liters. We add the hook which is around 100 ml of volume.

data.description: A durable tool consisting of a sturdy fiberglass shaft tipped with a set of 3 hooks, one large opposed by two small.  Hot sticks are used to maintain some standoff distance when manual manipulation of explosives is necessary, and robot assistance is unavailable.
A shaft with a pair of hooks on one end and a pry bar on the other, forged from a single piece of steel.

A long wicker fish trap made from bark, reeds, cordage, or other natural materials.  It's a staple fishing tool in many pre-industrial societies.  The principle of action: the fish swims inside to eat the bait, but can't get out.
A simple metal fishing hook.
An improvised fishing hook carved from wood or bone.

A professional fishing rod with a matching set of weights.  With this, you should be able to catch 'em all.

data.description: A commercial hand fishing reel.  It is a short rod with a section on one end with fishing line wrapped around it, with a rotating guard around that.  It is not as effective as a normal fishing pole, but is much more compact.

A small hand press for hand loading firearm ammunition.  It comes with everything you need to start hand loading your own munitions.

A collection of items improvised for field reloading of shotshells.  A plank with a hole cut in the center, a medium-sized nail, and a whittled dowel are used to seat wads, decap primers, and (carefully!) reprime hulls.  Powder and shot are measured with a cut-down shotshell hull.  The opposite side of the plank has been shaped to allow for roll-crimping of the plastic hulls.  There's no provision for resizing, so reloaded hulls will fire best in the firearm they were fired from.
A tool used for properly disassembling firearm ammunition.
The internal compartment for holding medium sized batteries, for a battery system bionic.
Integrated bionic tools implanted in your fingers.

Integrated soldering iron and screwdriver set.
A large stick with the end carved into a broad blade for digging.  It could be used to dig shallow pits, but not deep ones.
A small, sharp gardening shovel, perfect for digging up grubs and worms.
A farming implement.  You can use it to turn tillable land into a slow-to-cross pile of dirt, or dig a shallow pit.
A farming implement made from bronze.  The added heft and durability should let you till soil for farming more easily as well.

A crude shovel with a shovelhead made from wood, historically used as an alternative to metal shovels when metal was too expensive.  It works passably well, but really can't compare to a metal shovel.
A sturdy metal rake, a must-have during autumn.
A cheap plastic rake.  Will break quite quickly if used for anything other than raking leaves.
An old-fashioned farming tool used to cut tall grass.  Despite being a giant blade on the end of a stick, it is incredibly awkward to use for anything but its intended purpose.
A digging tool.  Use it to dig pits adjacent to your location.
A sturdy metal shovel used for picking up snow and moving it somewhere else.  It was useful before the cataclysm, but now it's useless.
A cheap plastic shovel used for picking up snow and moving it somewhere else.  It was useful before the cataclysm, but now it's useless.
A primitive tool for cutting grass.  The sharp, crescent-shaped stone at the end of the handle is barely good enough for the job.
An old-fashioned farming tool for cutting tall grass.
A handheld grass-cutting tool with a cast bronze blade, fastened to a wood handle wrapped with leather.

A cordless, double-sided, gasoline-powered hedge trimmer.  A long line of sharp-edged teeth extends from the engine; turning the trimmer on will make them rapidly vibrate.  The poor man's chainsaw as far as the zombies are concerned.

This makes it a lot easier to feel confident that the chemical you've made is what you think it is.

data.description: A hot plate with a metal housing attached.  The metal housing has a magnification viewport and a slot into which a capillary tube containing a crystallized sample is inserted.  The device lets you precisely measure the melting point of a crystal, a property very useful in identifying what it is and how pure it is.

data.description: A classic tool for the ages!  This hefty, durable piece of lab equipment makes small things look bigger.  Without electricity the light doesn't work, but the rest of it is surprisingly functional.  Unfortunately it's not useful for very much at the moment.

This microscope has less magnification than a standard one.  It's also stereoscopic and produces a neat 3-D image of the surface.  It was typically used for performing dissections and other fine-detail work on small creatures.  It still works pretty well with an added light source, but what would you do with it?

This thing doesn't look much like a funnel.  It's a teardrop-shaped piece of glass with a stopper at the wide end and a valve at the other.  It can be used to wash one liquid with another, like water and an oil, and then draw off whichever of the two liquids contains a higher amount of whatever compound you're trying to isolate.  With a high level of skill, it can also be used to make juvenile farting noises.
A tall glass column with a stopcock at the end.  If you're serious about chemistry, you probably have a tattoo of one of these somewhere.

Just looking at this thing makes you feel like a proper mad scientist.  It's a series of glass tubes and round flasks, connected to a central motor and a heating element.  The heating element warms one flask, kept rotating by the motor, evaporating the contents.  The vapor is then condensed in the tubes and collected in another flask, in case you wanted to save it for later.

One of the classic pieces of mad science glassware, this is a small-volume still that passes vapor through a fractional distillation column and then condenses the distillate in a cooled collection column.  A grad student or a robot (is there really any difference?) collects the distillate in fractions so that specific contents can be analyzed.  Going a few milliliters at a time, it would not be very effective to try to distill whiskey in this thing.

A set of plastic trays, electrodes, and a power supply designed to create an electric voltage gradient through a liquid solution containing a solid gel.  Stuff like proteins and DNA would then get separated on the gel according to electrical charge and size.  Pretty useless now for anything but salvage.

A smaller, benchtop version of the larger furniture-sized centrifuge.  Don't be fooled by its portable scale; it's still a very powerful piece of equipment that can spin stuff really quickly.  It's not a toy!
Stop giggling.  This is a tiny plastic valve, get your mind out of the gutter.
A plastic box with holes in it.  Not that exciting, unless you're desperate for a place to store a test tube.  Then it's great.
A plastic tray riddled with small holes, for storing microcentrifuge tubes.
A heavy metal plate and a sturdy rod, for clamping lab stuff to.

data.description: Also called storm glass or 'Goethe barometer', The weather glass barometer consists of a glass container with a sealed body, half filled with water. data.description: A pallet of humble mud bricks that have dried for a week while you were out risking your life.  Disassemble it to retrieve your frame and building supplies.
A bulky device that turns water and calcium carbide into unpressurized acetylene.
A power tool that spins a disc at high speed to cut or polish metal.
A manufactured disc for an angle grinder, with a thin, abrasive edge designed for cutting metal.
A manufactured disc for an angle grinder, with a thick, abrasive surface designed for grinding and shaping metal.
A pair of toothy wooden paddles used to clean fibers for use in textile production.
A homemade vacuum-forming machine with an air pump.  It's used for creating plastic molds.
A vacuum-forming machine with an air pump.  It's used for creating plastic molds.
A tool similar to a chisel, designed to remove paint.
A metal clamp, useful for holding things in place, especially if you have several of them.
A small prying tool with a clawed bend at one end for pulling spikes.  Use it to open locked doors without destroying them or to lift manhole covers.  You could also wield it to bash some heads in.

data.description: A portable concrete mixer.  It is large and heavy, but it can be operated solo.  Unfold to use.

data.description: A cordless battery-powered drill with a selection of drill bits.
A black power drill with a selection of bits.  Uses a power cord, so it will have to be plugged into a power grid or vehicle to function.

A cordless battery-powered impact wrench, designed to deliver high torque via an internal rotating hammer.  It comes with a standard set of sockets, and makes a loud ratcheting sound when it operates.  You could use it to turn large bolts or change a vehicle wheel.
