data.dynamic_line: I guess so."  They beam sheepishly.  "Uh, call me Cranberry.  Cran is fine too.  It's nice to meet someone else from here.  I guess having some company for once wouldn't be awful.

responses.text: I guess I could stay for a while.
Actually, I have some places to be right now.  Good to meet you.

data.dynamic_line: Not a whole lot, really.  They made me track down and destroy some government documents a while back.  Obviously I read them first, but it wasn't much.  As far as I know, this place had an experimental computer network before everything went to hell.  What's going on in there now is anybody's guess.

Yeah!  Crazy shit.  They sent me to an office building to find a folder with a certain serial and get rid of it.  They didn't even care what was on it.  By the time I got there, though, the building was pretty much a wreck.  The folder had been sitting in a puddle for God knows how long, and there was nothing even remotely legible by then.

That's what the news said, anyway.  It was only about a 20-minute trip from my apartment and sometimes I'd drive past it, so I was curious and I did some research into it.  The only info I could find about it online said that it was a NASA lab for computer research, but that was probably bullshit.  I mean, do you see any NASA logos?  Sure, we got huge steel doors and 15-foot concrete walls, but not a logo in sight.  The building probably goes underground, right?  It's way too small to be a whole laboratory up here.
Just trying to get some rest.  I don't have anywhere else to stay, so they let me sleep on the couch out here as long as I keep my gun handy.

responses.text: They don't let you in to sleep?

data.dynamic_line: Dude, I wish.  It sounds like there's different people on the mic at different times, but all of them give me the same spiel: nobody's allowed in right now.  I guess I shouldn't raise a fuss about it, honestly.  All being considered, this compound is pretty safe, and the couch ain't so bad.

dynamic_line.gendered_line: Yeah.  Have you noticed how they pay us in these tiny little gold coins?"  Cranberry holds one up for emphasis.  "It's bizarre.  You'd think they have a gold mine in there, but no, they don't, so they make me cross the damn world grabbing gold bars.  As far as scrip goes, it seems inconvenient as hell to make.

responses.text: Now that you mention it, it does seem rather strange.

dynamic_line: Thinking I should go hunt something soon…
Just wondering if things will get better someday.
Hmm?  Nothing, I guess I just like resting in this place.  I feel good today.

dynamic_line.gendered_line: Have you ever noticed how… wait no, never mind.

dynamic_line: Wondering if the whole world is like this now.  It has to be, right?  I was watching some foreign news channels when everything was going down, and it sounded like things were just as bad there…

dynamic_line.gendered_line: Hey, did you notice that there's working wi-fi here?  Not that anything else is online anymore, but still.

dynamic_line: Just vibing.

data.dynamic_line: *goes quiet.  They chew their lip, looking off towards a point in space.
No, no!  It's fine, promise.  It's just been a hot minute, and I'm trying to remember it.  It's been a while.  You sure you want to hear it?

responses.text: I might not have the time.  Hold that thought for later.

data.dynamic_line: *stares at a point at the wall, thinking.  Their wedding ring glints on their left hand.
…Alright.  Well.  For starters, I lived alone in an apartment, and I didn't have any family or relatives I really cared about, so things were a lot easier for me than they could have been.

I've never really been a prepper, but I was into conspiracy theories.  Not as a participant, just as an observer.  I think information spread is interesting."  They pause.  "I think it was in early March that I started thinking something was wrong.  Like, the riots were bad beforehand, right?  And that just seemed like normal unrest.  But then suddenly you're seeing it happening in other countries where the normal explanations don't work.  So I dug deeper, and once I did, I realized that this had been happening since January, and getting worse since then.  That was when I started to take it seriously.

But like, I was a park ranger.  I wasn't exactly making six figures, and you know how bad rent was.  I couldn't buy a ton of canned food, but what I *could* do is can things myself.  Not in tin cans, but in jars; the old way.  So every paycheck, I'd use a little bit to buy one or two big glass jars, and on the weekends I'd spend a few hours filling them up with food and sealing them.  I started brushing up at the range too.  Proud gun owner, baby.

I bought fruit and veggies from the store for my greens, but I figured those didn't really have enough calories for the long-term, so I hunted.  To be more accurate, I poached in the park I worked at.  It was never anything huge; I had to be able to conceal this stuff, remember.  But we were on a shoestring budget as it is and we never had the people we needed, so it was trivial to bag an animal using a rifle from one of the ranger stations.  I'd dress the carcass, then leave it in a place that I could either bring with me in my truck that day or come back later to sneak it out.  I never got caught.  I'm not proud of it, but I'm not really ashamed of it, either.  Besides, venison is great.

So I figured that this wasn't going to be a problem a few months down the line, right?  Just a flash in the pan.  I had my emergency stock of food in case things went bad for a little while.  Best case scenario, I never have to worry about it, things go back to normal after a bit, and I save some money on groceries for a while.  And I wanted to keep doing this for a few more weeks, but…

March 30th happened."  Cranberry seems shaken, and talks a little louder for a second.  "You remember that video, right?  That was what set off alarm bells in my head.  That shit was fucking scary.  And at that point I realized, okay, I think things are about to get bad and this is for real.

Whoo-ee, someone was living under a rock, huh?  It was all over the news.  Video on YouTube, it was a livestream of one of the riots in Minneapolis.  A mom was…"  They hesitate.  "I don't want to go into detail, but it was real bad.  Real bad.  That's what set off people panicking.

People started freaking out.  I did, too.  I don't know how bad things got elsewhere, but shit was flying off the shelves where I lived.  Empty racks at grocery stores everywhere you looked.  I had enough food for a few weeks, so it wasn't a problem for me, but it still shook me up bad.  Every day some horrible new shit was happening somewhere in the world, and things got just worse and worse.  Then that insanity with Rhode Island happened, and once the national emergency came out, I knew that okay, this is happening, it's actually happening."

"Did you know that I was still going to work that entire time?  I don't know, it just felt meditative.  I lived in a pretty rural area, so there wasn't the kind of chaos in the cities and congestion on the roads.  I could just take a side road there and have a day of quiet.  Just the woods and whoever else actually bothered to show up that day.  The park closed for visitors closed a day or two before the state of emergency, and it was really peaceful, being there alone.

Then the portals happened, and you know the rest from there.  Two days later, the world was over.  There was a lot of chaos in my complex.  I just nailed shut my front door, drew all the curtains, kept my shotgun loaded, and probably slept maybe ten hours total that week.  I don't know if there was someone up in the sky watching over me, but if there was, I sure as hell owe them big time.

I kind of lost track of the days.  Every day was the same; eat, check the barricades, look on the Internet, play some games with the sound off to try and distract myself.  I filled up my bathtub, and once the water went out, I'd drink from there when I needed to hydrate.  Meal planning got easier after I was down to just my canned stuff.  The Internet didn't stay on for long, though, which I guess was a blessing because of how many people were sharing their fear and awful experiences in real time.  I did that routine every day until that emergency broadcast came through that no help was coming, and then I knew it was over.

It took a bit for me to muster the nerve to leave, but I wanted to.  Had to see, y'know?  It was… a shock, zombies just walking in the parking lot.  Like, sure, I could look out the window, but it feels different up close.  I had my knife handy, and I didn't want to make too much noise, so that's what I used.  I stabbed one of my dead neighbors in the neck that day."  They smile wistfully.  "I threw up on my shoes after the first one, but it got easier.

My truck was still there, and was on half a tank of gas.  I thought, okay, this isn't gonna be easy, but I can pack my food and the things I need to take with me into the truck, and then drive to that building I know about that was so reinforced."  They gesture around them.  "This building.  The Hub.  So I got some stuff into a bugout bag in the cabin and filled up the truck bed, and off I went.  The roads were bad, but I'm not a bad driver.  Zombies are slow.

If only, huh?  No, not quite.  About five miles away I hit a bad pothole and skidded off the road and got stuck.  That's not a problem on its own, but a few minutes into trying to get it unstuck, I saw a big furrow of dirt coming towards me and decided, you know what, maybe I should get off the side of the road.  So I grab my bugout bag from the cabin and a little food from the bed, and I book it onto the road.  Now, I don't know what this thing was, but it hit the truck from below and *flipped it over*.  That was enough to make me say 'Nope, I can go on foot.'

It took me a few days from there.  I had a heavy load, and it was slow going.  I slept on the road the first night because I was so freaked out by what I saw, but the day after I got the nerves to walk through the woods.  I had a tent, so it wasn't so bad.  Every now and then, I'd run into a zombie, or a wrecked car that still had some of them buckled in.  I left my shotgun behind in the truck, so I got better at using the knife.  It gets easier, y'know?

A while later, I made it here.  The gate was open, so I just walked right in.  I tried the intercom, but nobody answered, which I'm sure you had happen to you, too.  Then I realize: this building is super reinforced, unlocked, and seems abandoned now.  Why don't I just stay here?  So I set up my stuff in this here lobby and I spend the night there.  Then I try the intercom again.

Hoo boy, yes they did, and let me tell you, they were not happy campers about me crashing on their couch.  Now, these people don't tell me who they are, but they tell me to get off the premises immediately.  I wasn't having that.  I had been through hell and come out the other end, and I don't remember what I said to them, but it was along the lines of 'I have nowhere to go, and your building is nice and cozy, so if you want me to leave, you can come out here and make me.'"  They laugh.  "They weren't expecting me to bite back.  So I turn off the intercom and I go eat lunch.  When I go back again, the first thing they ask is if I want a job.

Well, no.  It was obvious they just wanted to get rid of me, but I decided I wanted to show that I was useful.  They tell me to find a crashed drone somewhere in the surrounding area and bring it back here.  No directions, of course.  Y'know, go find this drone in the middle of the woods, it'll be easy.  But I had some tools in my bag, right?  And yours truly has repaired some drones in the park service."

"So it takes me a whole-ass afternoon, but I find their stupid drone stuck in a tree.  I can see the camera's still on, so I pick it up and I tell the lens: 'Hey, you want me to fix it too?'  And I do.  It was just a cracked frame and the wiring to the rotors was sliced up.  The propellers themselves were fine.  So I bring it out of the woods and turn it off.  Then I open up the casing, solder up the wires, and use superglue to hold the frame together, which wasn't perfect, but I figured it'd hold until it got back home.  Then I turned it back on, and wouldn't you know, it immediately starts up and sits there for a minute, like 'What the fuck?  Why am I working again?'  And then it flies away, and I walk my smug ass back home.

You got it."  Cranberry grins.  "I ask them if their drone got home in one piece, and it did.  They said that my work wasn't bad at all and did a little impromptu interview asking where I learned my skills and how I got to the building.  I got the canned intro of 'we underestimated your usefulness', and like you say, the rest is history.  Now we're here.

responses.text: That's quite the story.  You seem to be feeling pretty good, in spite of the world ending.

data.dynamic_line:
I guess I am, yeah.  It feels nice to be putting all my skills to use instead of working an underpaid job to walk around the same woods flying a quadcopter around and being a glorified PR rep to cranky parents who are only at the park because they promised their kids they'd go.  Mind you, I'd still go back to it if I could."  Their expression falters a little.  "We all had our struggles, but things are different now, you know?  We get to worry about the future in a whole new way; an existential way that we never had to consider before, not really.  Sure, there was the occasional nuke scare, but as a society, we had things pretty good.  Unless the dead stop getting back up, I… don't think things are going to ever go back to normal."

Cranberry pauses for a moment, then shakes it off.  "But… right now, I'm feeling at peace with everything, despite it all.  Maybe I'm just in shock, and it'll all come crashing down one of these days.  Things might get worse, and they may never get better.  But I feel alright.  And I think that's enough for me.
*smiles at you, genuine and warm.  "It feels nice to tell it.  You're welcome."
I'm sorry, that's a bit personal.  Like, you seem alright, but that's kind of heavy stuff, y'know?  Maybe I can tell you another time.

I guess I am, yeah.  Feels like a stupid chore."  They suddenly pause.  "Hey.  If you happen across any gold out in the world, I'll pay you to bring it back for me.  Right now my assignment stipulates eight scrip per kilo, and I'd be willing to give you all of that.  I just want something else to do.  Just maybe don't mention it to the intercom, alright?  This is supposed to be my job.

no.yes: &The intercom is silent.
no.no: &An intercom is embedded into the wall here, just next to the card reader.  It's a metal box about as big as a dinner plate, with a speaker shaped like a downwards curve and a large camera prominently featured in the center.  You see a single metal button with a dark LED next to it.  The intercom is silent.

data.//: This is the generic 'services' menu for Hub 01, but a lot of dialogue leads back here.  The other IDs here are used to defined custom responses that make sense within the context of the dialogue they stem from; you can find most of them in other files.

no: Ugh, I hate intercom duty… oh, um.  Hello.
What's up with the interference in this thing?
dynamic_line.//: higher faction trust results in warmer greetings
yes: Hello again.  Brought us anything good?
&The voice on the intercom is humming a tune.
What's up with the interference in this thing?

responses.text: The traders at the refugee center asked me to deliver this drive of FEMA data…
You mentioned you had a map of the area?

data.dynamic_line: You may rarely come across certain items which have been affected by the…ongoing phenomena.  They may seem like mundane household objects, but exhibit properties which seem to defy casual explanation.  I'm afraid that we cannot be clearer on this matter - suffice to say that you will likely know it when you see it.  We are willing to barter for these items at a high value.

dynamic_line.yes: &The intercom is silent.
dynamic_line.no: &The intercom crackles with static as it turns on.  The LED next to the button lights up a bright red, and the camera lens whirrs as it focuses on you.  There is no immediate response.

responses.text: [Tap the camera lens.]  Look, I know someone's listening.  What is this place?
The merchant at the refugee center sent me.  You were looking for a hard drive from them?
The traders mentioned you were looking for help.

data.dynamic_line: &The intercom hisses.  A voice of indeterminate sex speaks flatly.  "I don't know who you are or how you got to this location, but we have nothing to gain from one another.  If you have a reason to be here, then please state your business.  Otherwise, please leave the area."

responses.text: I have a delivery from the Free Merchants.  You requested a hard drive from them.
You do realize that the front door is just open?
It's the apocalypse out here!  Please just let me in!
I'm just looking for valuables.  Maybe we can trade?
Look, there must be something we can work out.

data.dynamic_line: &The intercom is silent.

I promise you, there is nothing you can do for us.  Now leave, before I'm forced to-"  They stop suddenly.  You hear a short, muffled conversation from the other end.  There's a brief pause.  "Alright.  We might be able to gain some mutual benefit.  It's a dangerous task, but if you complete it then we would be willing to open up limited trading access.

responses.text: Risk my neck for the privilege of trading with you?  Maybe another time.

data.dynamic_line: Right.  Your handling of this situation was exemplary, and it's clear to us that we greatly underestimated our potential for mutual benefit.  If you are interested, we are willing to offer you more work going forward, and all of it will have proper compensation from now on.

responses.text: And the trading we agreed on?

data.dynamic_line: Certainly.  I've just finished speaking with a certain individual, who has authorized you limited access to a selection of our internal stores.  We will provide you with pay for contracts in the form of tokens to be used as an exchange currency, which you can then trade for goods.  We are also amenable to bartering in exchange for supplies that are currently difficult for us to obtain from outside the facility, and are especially interested in any…especially unusual items you may find.

responses.text: I'll keep that in mind.  Let's get down to business.

data.dynamic_line: We look forward to working with you.

data.//: These are all dialogues related to the breadcrumb quest from the refugee center to deliver a hard drive.

dynamic_line.yes: &The intercom's tray wordlessly slides open.
dynamic_line.no: &The intercom erupts into static.  Then, it resolves into a voice.  It clears its throat, then speaks slowly and carefully.  "Understood.  There is a tray embedded beneath the intercom.  Please place the drive into it."  On cue, a small portion of the wall beneath the intercom slides out along rails, revealing a large tray several inches deep.  "You are welcome to leave afterwards."

responses.text: Hold on, who are you?  And what do you want with the data?
What am I getting out of this?
Sorry, forgot to grab the drive.  I'll return with it.

data.dynamic_line: &The intercom is silent.
Ask Gavin.
&The tray slides shut.  "Thank you."  The intercom turns off without another word.

data.//: This exchange is used when the player is already a mercenary for Hub 01, so the intercom is much more informal about it
data.dynamic_line: Oh!  Good.  We had written that off as a non-starter.  Just drop it into the tray and we'll bring it in.

responses.text: I don't have the drive with me right now; I'll give it to you when I have it.

data.dynamic_line: Thank you.  Was there anything else you needed?

data.//1: This is the main talk topic for all of the intercom's contracts.  The player is able to learn more about missions here, and accept new ones.
data.//2: This also contains dialogue topics to complete one-time missions.  Repeatables are handled in 'robofac_intercom_trades.json' instead.
data.dynamic_line: What would you like to discuss?

responses.text: I'm back from the convoy.  [Hand over the hard case.]
I'm back from LIXA.  [Hand over the data.]
I found it.  I found your template.  [Hand over the silicon photonics template.]
The weapon worked!  [Hand over the inactive trifacet.]
I found the robot, but…  [Hand over the trifacet remains.]
Do you have any more work for me right now?

data.dynamic_line: Give me a moment to look at your file… here we are.  Valid assignments are turning up empty at the moment.  I'm afraid we have no open contracts for you.

data.//: This mission is assigned and completed using conditions in dialogue with the intercom. As such, we don't have any goal, which would make it auto-complete under certain circumstances.
data.description: Investigate a nearby field and return with Dr. Prado and the robot prototype she was testing.  Failing that, retrieve the I/O recorder stored within the robot.  If the robot remains operational, avoid direct confrontation and use EMP grenades to disable it.

dialogue.//: All dialogue for most of the intercom's missions is handled through talk_topics; we don't use these strings for those such missions

data.dynamic_line: One of our scientists recently left the building to perform a field test of a prototype robot, but failed to return.  We have not been able to contact them.  Your job would be to investigate the testing site, and return with her and the prototype.  Failing that, return with the data recorder that was attached to our prototype.

responses.text: That seems trivial.  Is there a catch?

data.dynamic_line: There is.  If the robot is operational, it's very likely to be hostile and extremely dangerous.  I don't recommend fighting it directly.  Dr. Prado left the building with a handful of EMP grenades.  If you can locate those grenades, use them to disable the prototype instead.

responses.text: I'll do it.  Where is the test site?
Extremely dangerous?  What kind of danger should I expect?
I'll pass on getting killed today, thanks.

data.dynamic_line: It's built with experimental combat programming and some heavy-duty armor.  Despite the armor, it's pretty nimble, so unless you've got a vehicle don't expect to outrun it.  We decided to hold off on adding long-range weapons until we finished the initial field testing, so if you can keep your distance, you should be safe.

responses.text: I can handle it.  Where is the test site?

data.dynamic_line: Very close by."  The voice lists off some relative coordinates.  "Good luck.
You're back.  Do you have anything to report?

responses.text: Your scientist was dead, but I disabled the prototype.  Is this what you were looking for?  [Hand over the prototype I/O recorder.]
Not yet.  I'll get back to it.

data.dynamic_line: &The intercom is silent for a few seconds while the tray slides back in.  "Yes it is.  It's unfortunate that only the data was salvageable, but you have our thanks for returning it nonetheless."

responses.text: Alright, I've done my part.  What now?
Is "unfortunate" how you usually describe someone being eviscerated by a robot?

data.dynamic_line: Dr. Prado knew the risks, and she chose to follow through with the test anyway.  Her death is cause for sadness, and it will affect us, but you didn't even know her.  At least now, something of her work will remain.

&The voice hesitates.  "About that.  Give me a moment."  After a pause, you hear muffled back-and-forth conversation.  You can't make out what's being said, but you can make out at least two other distinct voices.

data.description: Find the corpse of a Hub 01's AI researcher and retrieve the hard case they brought with them during the evacuation.

data.dynamic_line:
When the portal storms started, the government issued an evacuation order for critical personnel and sent convoys to retrieve them, with our head of AI research among the recalled.  We recently discovered that he died when the convoy transferring him was ambushed in the initial chaos, but his corpse and belongings might remain intact enough to benefit from his research."

"We want you to travel to the convoy and locate the body, if possible.  His evacuation protocol included retrieving and storing as much of the data from his facility as possible, to be stored in a code-locked hard case.  If this hard case is present, retrieve it, and bring it back here."

"We offer the standard hazard pay of 4 HGC for this contract.

responses.text: I'll take it.  Where's the convoy?
What should I expect to go up against?
Who was this person, and what do they look like?
What else do you have available?

data.dynamic_line: The convoy was composed of vehicles and personnel from the US Army, and it was heavily armed.  Our surveillance of the area has shown that the majority of the slain military personnel have revivified.  Resistance will be heavy, but if possible, you may be able to locate and retrieve the hard case, then exfiltrate without direct combat as long as you can outpace the undead there.  Otherwise, bring a rifle and plenty of ammo.
Officially speaking, they were a senior DARPA researcher.  Their corpse should stick out; it's likely the only one not wearing camouflage.  That's all you need to know.
It was ambushed on the road."  The intercom recites a series of coordinates.  "Report back with the hard case.  If the researcher brought it with him, it will be intact; have no doubt about that.

&The intercom's tray slides shut.

"This is the case; thank you.  Transferring the stipulated amount now."  The tray slides back open with your payment.  "As an additional form of payment, you have been given clearance to receive a map of the area around this site, to assist in your work.  The standing price is 1 HGC; please inform us if you'd like to follow up on that offer going forward.

responses.text: [PER 8] The original markings on that case had been scratched out.  Who did it really belong to?

data.dynamic_line: &The intercom is silent.

data.description: Reach the collapsed tower basement, and search the ruins for a photonic circuitry template.  The intercom warned you about heavy enemy presence, and of the existence of a hazardous environment.

data.dynamic_line:
Our facility once sourced advanced photonic circuitry from a nearby robotics manufacturer.  Their building suffered major damage during the portal storms, and collapsed almost entirely.  However, preliminary scouting reveals that the basement prototyping lab likely remains intact."

"We ask you to investigate the ruins, and if possible, retrieve a template for the fabrication of said photonic circuitry."

"Completion of this contract awards 8 HGC, the standard heightened-hazard rate.  We are also willing to provide you with a set of protective gear at a considerable discount upon acceptance of the contract.

responses.text: Let's do this, then.  Transfer the location.
You mention hazard pay.  What dangers are there?
What else do you have available?

data.dynamic_line:
I don't believe I'm cleared to-"  You hear brief chatter.  "Apologies; I was mistaken.  The manufacturer was, technically speaking, kept secret from the public.  As a result, it operated using an office tower as a front, and was located underground.  An elevator in the back of the building led to the basement, but it was likely destroyed in the damage - as a result, you will need to find a way down yourself.  While there were stairs as well, it's highly likely that they have been destroyed."

"We advise bringing a way to safely enter and exit the lower level; a grappling hook would work well for this purpose.  Given the damage, the elevator shaft itself probably remains intact, and would be your likeliest point of entry to the underground portion of the building.

About that."  You hear papers shuffling.  "Our drones are unable to approach the structure too closely, as a large amount of interference prevents surveillance, but long-distance measurements reveal a high concentration of toxic compounds in the air, as well as densely-clustered heat signatures.  We expect a high concentration of undead, and other dangers are likely.

responses.text: Tell me about these heat signatures.
"Other dangers" is a little vague.  Do you have anything more substantial?

data.dynamic_line: Correct.  The source of the chemicals is unknown, as is the exact composition; only trace amounts are present in the air itself.  We can, however, extrapolate that something within the ruins is creating highly poisonous emissions.  We do not know how strong these emissions will become, or what form they will take.

At the moment, their origin is unclear.  The temperature profile of the building is highly unusual, despite the damage, and is much denser than wandering hordes observed through remote scouting.  A large amount of heat consistent with an extremely high density of organisms appears to be emanating from the basement itself.  We are, unfortunately, in the dark about the cause of this density.  We would advise you remain observant and note down any abnormalities.

To be specific, there have been anomalous readings that we are unable to explain.  Seismic disturbances have been recorded emanating from the ruins, with a magnitude ranging from two to four, and periodic vocalizations have been documented to exceed 150 decibels.  We are uncertain why or how these phenomena are created.

responses.text: The more I hear about this, the worse it sounds.

data.dynamic_line: Did you have any other concerns?

Your hesitation is understandable.  Unfortunately, we have already taken all possible measures to obtain data and information remotely, but we are unable to develop our understanding further without a physical presence.

Excellent.  Thank you very much."  The intercom recites a series of coordinates.  "Exercise a great deal of caution.  We do not know what the conditions on the ground are like.  Use your best judgment.  As before, we are willing to offer you protective gear, if you would like it.

responses.text: I would like that gear, yes.  Tell me about it.

data.dynamic_line: Fantastic."  The intercom's tray slides shut, and then opens shortly afterwards with your payment.  "You have our thanks and our payment.

responses.text: Do you have any idea what I just went through?
You certainly gave me a run for my money, I'll say that much.

data.dynamic_line: As we discussed during acceptance of the contract, we were aware of hazardous ground conditions, but we were unable to deduce further information other than what was available through long-range sensing.  If you would like to provide a description of the hazards present, we are willing to document them.

responses.text: [Detail the conditions at the collapsed tower and its basement.  This will advance time by ten minutes.]
[Let them know how bad that mission REALLY was.]
…Just forget it.  Let's never speak of this again.

data.dynamic_line:
&Over the course of several minutes, you explain what happened at the ruins: the zombie presence and gigantic tendrils on the surface, and the biological infestation completely taking over the basement, as well as the hostile threats encountered therein.  The voice periodically interjects with questions or statements; the whole time, you hear the sounds of typing on a keyboard.

"We would like to extend our thanks for your detailed report.  It is clear to us that the threat level present at the manufacturer was far higher than we had originally anticipated, and your performance in the situation was exemplary.  Should you desire further contract work, we will bear these facts in mind, and ensure that the threat prognoses of your future assignments are adequately assessed."

responses.text: It's fine.  At least now we know for the future.

data.dynamic_line: &The intercom waits patiently.

responses.text: Description, huh?  Where to begin?  Let's start with the giant mob of zombies that was infesting the building.  Oh, and there were also horrors full of toxic gas that exploded when I got near them or killed one, so I was constantly choking on fumes the whole time.

data.dynamic_line: That makes-

responses.text: Oh, but that's not all!  They were coming from a pair of giant fucking tentacles coming out of the ground like a monster movie that were constantly roaring and shaking the whole building, and toxic exploding spiders kept crawling off and shooting poison darts at me until I got away or stopped the tentacles themselves, which wasn't easy because the entire building had come down around them.

data.dynamic_line: What do you mean by-

responses.text: Then it took me half an hour to find the way down, because there were holes in the floor everywhere, and when I finally did, I was in the insides of a goddamn flesh pit with flooding up to my ankles, and to complement the innards hanging from the ceiling that I couldn't see through the gas that would throw me ten feet and make me start drowning, there were dozens of people fused together in lumps everywhere, and did I mention the poison gas?  Because they were full of it too, and so everything reeked and it felt like being in a giant fucking intestine full of people.

data.dynamic_line: Please slow down-

responses.text: And after ALL THAT, I find your manufacturing lab on the other end of this thing straight out of a fever dream nightmare, and after ALL THAT, I find your photonics, and then I have to get ALL THE WAY out of the ENTIRE ZOMBIE-INFESTED TOWN so I could bring you your stupid fucking template.  Are you happy now?

data.dynamic_line: &The voice on the other side of the intercom is silent with disbelief.
…Uh.  We are- thank you for finding the photonics.  We will, ah, make sure that the threat conditions of your future contracts are adequately assessed.  Um.  Thank you.

data.description: Disable and retrieve the unusual robot by <color_yellow>successfully stunning it with the provided hm12 dazzle rifle or a scrambler grenade,</color> then <color_yellow>quickly running up and deactivating the robot before it recovers from the stun</color>.  You can keep shooting it while it's stunned to prolong the time until it is active again.  You can intercept the robot indicated by Hub 01, or find an inactive robot somewhere else.  <color_yellow>You'll need some experience in electronics or mechanics to disable it</color>.

data.//: 'SM' is short for 'side mission'. These contracts are separate from Hub 01's main quests.
data.dynamic_line:
One of our scout drones spotted a partially-malfunctioning robot of unconventional make while tracking an anomalous radiation spike close by.  We project that much knowledge could be gained from a close examination of this subject, and you would be tasked to retrieve it for us intact.  We will equip you with a prototype rifle and instructions on how to use it and deactivate the robot, if you accept."

"The success of this contract requires that the subject be brought back in an inactive state, and *not* destroyed.  A ruined robot is of no scientific value.  We emphasize that you use the hm12 to complete this task, though it will likely be a diffcult shot to make.  A scrambler grenade might also suffice, but an EMP blast would likely destroy the target outright."

"Completion of this contract awards 2 HGC, and you will be able to keep the hm12 rifle and the equipment used to operate it.

responses.text: You've got a deal.  I'll track down your robot.
What is this robot, and what does it look like?
What else do you have available?

data.dynamic_line:
If you'll give me a moment…"  You hear the sounds of typing.  "Its designation is hm12, you may have seen it in the news.  It is a weapon which is mostly harmless to living targets, but is specifically designed to incapacitate robots without harming their internals.  Once a subject is stunned, it can be manually deactivated; That is, you must approach it and turn it off before it reactivates."

"A shot will only stun the robot if you manage to hit its main sensory array, which will require good aim.  In short, try to use the weapon to stun it, then run up to it and examine it to find the, er, off switch.

We are as of yet uncertain of its origin and purpose.  Its body most closely resembles a pyramid on what we believe are three sets of legs for mobility.  It is lightly armed, and has attacked our cam-spy drones using high-voltage electric discharge.  We theorize that this is most likely for deterrence, and not to cause direct harm.  Nonetheless, we need to emphasize that its full capabilities are unknown, and we do not know how it will react when confronted with a living threat.

Lovely.  Just a moment; we will transfer the hm12 and handling procedures, which includes information of its last recorded location."

The intercom tray thumps several times as objects are placed into it.  After about a minute, it slides open, revealing a slender weapon that looks a bit like a radar gun, a heavy battery, a sheaf of papers in a binder, and a power bank.  "The hm12 draws power from a power bank, ensure it is charged before engaging.  Please remember to bring the specimen back *intact* - battered salvage is of no use to us.  To safely perform the task of deactivation, please review the provided documentation, and pay special attention to the procedures detailed in subsections IV and VII.

&The intercom tray quickly slides shut.

"We expected nothing less.  We hope you found the hm12's performance to be satisfactory."

responses.text: Will this weapon work on other robots, as well?
The handling procedures you gave me seemed to predate the Cataclysm.  How long had that robot been here?

data.dynamic_line: Yes, almost certainly.  UGVs, autonomous CROWS units, manhacks, and other drones should all be vulnerable to the weapon, although we advise great caution; as you might have found, it can be difficult to precisely hit the target.

Pardon me."  The voice briefly turns away from the microphone and asks something.  "Very well.  I am cleared to tell you that it appeared near the beginning of the portal storms, and during this time, it was logged and documented.  No attempt was ever made to retrieve it before the government collapsed.  That is all I am able to share with you at this time.

&The intercom tray quickly slides shut.  After a pause, the voice on the other end sighs.

"…we requested that the subject remain intact.  This outcome is… unfortunate.  We will process the specimen, but it is unlikely that it will yield usable information as to its purpose."

"You may keep the dazzle rifle.  You are dismissed."

data.description: Reach the LIXA facility, and search the area for anything of interest.  The intercom warned you about a number of undead aboveground, and the high probability of more underground.

data.dynamic_line:
During the Cataclysm, we lost contact with one of our sister sites, LIXA.  Aerial surveillance indicates that the facility's inhabitants are deceased, and beyond the now-zombified security detail, the site should be sparsely populated.  We want you to enter the facility and make a copy of what they were researching on the provided thumb drive.  Additionally, we will be providing you with a keycard that should at the very least get you in the front door."

"We're offering a standard 5 HGC for successful retrieval of the data.  If that isn't enough of an incentive, we do have a manifest from before we lost contact with the facility showing a handful of specialized powered suits in inventory.  You are free to take any that are left.

responses.text: Alright, I'll see if I can't get that data for you.
What can you tell me about what they were doing there?
If I lose the ID card or the memory stick, what should I do?
What else do you have available?

data.dynamic_line: All I can tell you is that they were conducting cutting-edge research related to-" The intercom abruptly cuts off for several seconds before coming back on, the voice sounding apologetic, "Sorry, but as it turns out I'm not at liberty to divulge that information.
It's an acronym that stands for Laser Interferometer eXodimensional resonance Assay.

data.//: I feel like this could be phrased better.
data.dynamic_line: Well, the ID card wouldn't strictly speaking be necessary if you were to find some way of breaching the facility's security doors." The voice pauses for a moment, "But that said we only have the one ID card, so unless you're confident you can get in without it, please don't lose it.  As for the memory stick I would highly recommend you not lose that as portable drives with the required hardware security modules to interface with secure terminals are in short supply these days.  However there may very well be some on-site for you to scavenge if you're lucky.

data.//: Is it a semi-colon or colon that goes here? Man, idk.
data.dynamic_line: Transferring the items now."  The intercom tray slides open, revealing an ID card for the facility and what looks like a USB thumb drive.  "Again: please take care not to lose either of these since we can't exactly make more of them.

As we discussed during acceptance of the contract, we were aware of hazardous ground conditions, but we were unable to deduce further information other than what was available through long-range sensing.  If you would like to provide a description of the hazards present, we are willing to document them.

responses.text: [Detail the conditions at the research facility.  This will advance time by ten minutes.]
…Just forget it.  Let's never speak of this again.

data.dynamic_line:
&Over the course of several minutes, you calmly detail the events at the facility: the unexpected zombie presence underground, the anomalous nature of the experiment floor, and the encounter with the warped and hostile research staff trapped in the corridor.  Throughout, the voice interjects with questions, the sounds of typing filling the pauses.

"We appreciate your thorough report," the voice finally responds.  "Your handling of the circumstances was commendable considering the anomalous and unpredictable nature of the facility.  If you seek further contract work, rest assured, we'll take into account the potential for anomalous circumstances in future assignments and relay them accordingly."

responses.text: It's fine.  At least now we know for the future.

data.dynamic_line: Given the context of your assignment, we are willing to sell you a set of our protective gear - a gas mask and an environmental suit - at a considerable discount.  We will part with it for two exchange coins."  The intercom waits expectantly.  "Actually, hold on, we might not have one in your size…

responses.text: What will it do for me?
I have to give it a thought.

data.dynamic_line:
What the gas mask does should be obvious; we'll provide you with a cartridge, of course.  The environment suit is full-body, and protects you from water, harmful radiation, and environmental hazards.  It's also rated to protect from electric shocks of up to twelve thousand volts."

"Bear in mind that the suit isn't armor.  It will keep you safe from the environment, but it's just Nomex and it won't protect you from anything stronger than a punch.  The modular defense system is designed to fit over it, so I'd urge you to bring them both if fighting is unavoidable.
To assist your operations, we are willing to sell you a map of the local area, as surveyed by our cam-spy drones.  Its standing price is 1 HGC.

responses.text: I'll have to give it some thought.

Here's the rules.  The first and most important one: ALWAYS CLOSE THE FUCKING ENTRY DOOR BEHIND YOUR ASS!  If you're okay with that, the following rules are: don't fuck with us, don't steal from us, don't start a fight without a reason with someone from us.  Got it, punk?  Now get lost.

yes.gendered_line: I don't know if you know, but there are sewers underneath the prison. There was a flow of fresh air coming out of it, so I think it's leading to the surface.  It could be your way to freedom.  Feel free to use it.

responses.text: Yeah, I've been through situations far worse than that.
It was a nightmare, lots of <zombies>, blood everywhere!  Thank god I'm among living people again.

I don't know if I'll take your advice, but thanks nevertheless.
Wait, what?  A <swear> can of beans?!  I went through hell to get this <swear> thing for you, and all you give me as reward is a <swear> can of beans?!  I demand something more substantial.

data.dynamic_line: Huh, even so?  I'm not saying I approve your… tastes, but I definitely respect people who use all possibilities life has to offer.

responses.text: Yeah, we share the same opinions on this matter.

data.dynamic_line: Well, that's a boastful statement.  Not that I don't believe it, it's just….  Ah, nevermind.  Let's get to the point.  What do you want?

responses.text: I want to get out of this <swear> prison.  I hoped you could help me with that.

data.dynamic_line: Hold the horses, pal.  Nobody allowed you to stay here - yet.

responses.text: Please!  I don't want to go back there!  I'm tired and hungry!  I just need time to rest!
Shit!  Looks like I'm on my own now.  Thanks for nothing.  Bye.

data.dynamic_line: We don't have much space, and there's not much food.  Besides, I don't know you at all, and something tells me you won't survive another day.

responses.text: I guess I need to find some other place…

data.dynamic_line: The answer is still no.  In fact it might be better for us to kill you right away - you know, the less mouths to feed, the better.  But I'm in a good mood today, so I've decided to help you get out of this island.

responses.text: You know, I think I'll manage without your help.  Bye.

dynamic_line.no: I need you to retrieve some stuff from a locked safe.  Interested?
dynamic_line.yes: So, what are you waiting for?

responses.text: [Show the military ID card.] You mean this stuff?
What for do you need it?
I have a bad feeling about this.  Sorry, I'll pass.

data.dynamic_line: As I said, that's the thing I need.  You don't need to know what's that exactly.  Just grab all things you find in the safe, and call it a day.

responses.text: I have a bad feeling about this.  Sorry, I'll pass.

data.dynamic_line: Let's say that's none of your <swear> business.  Other questions?

responses.text: I have a bad feeling about this.  Sorry, I'll pass.

data.dynamic_line: Hey, where did you get it?  Nevermind, just give it to me.  Just <swear> now.

responses.text: Hey, no need to be hostile.  Here you go, I don't need it anyway.
I went through incredible hardships to get it.  Please, can I keep this to myself?
I killed tons of <zombies> while I was trying to get this thing.  Do you really think you and your handful of losers pose a threat to me?

data.dynamic_line: Okay.  It was convincing.  I'll still get what I want, one way or another.  You better watch your back from now on.
I'm afraid you're not in the position to demand anything from me, <name_b>.  <get_lost>

name.str: Get the military ID card from the chief's office

dialogue.offer: I need the military ID card from the chief's safe in his office.  I don't mean the warden, I mean the chief corrections officer, you hear me?  Just bring that thing to me and I'll help you.  Deal?
dialogue.accepted: Great!  Don't try to use the card now, just bring it straight to me.
dialogue.rejected: Fine, I'll get it sooner or later.
dialogue.advice: The chief's office is on the other side of the prison.  I think the road there is full of <zombies>, so you better find a weapon.  Also you probably will need some tools to crack the safe open.
dialogue.inquire: Did you get the card already?
dialogue.success: At last!  Give me a second to check if it isn't damaged.  Here, take this for your troubles.
dialogue.success_lie: Huh.  This isn't going to work like I thought.
dialogue.failure: You're useless.  I should've killed you when I met you.

data.//: Former miner, poor fellow succumbed to spiral madness.

data.dynamic_line: Spirals?

responses.text: Poor fellow - looks like you're out of your mind.  Can't help you, sorry.  I'm outta here.  Bye.

data.dynamic_line: <spirals>
<spirals>

responses.text: Why are you repeating 'spirals' over and over again?

data.dynamic_line: <spirals>
<spirals>

responses.text: Poor fellow - looks like you're out of your mind.  Can't help you, sorry.  I'm outta here.  Bye.

dialogue.describe: You wouldn't believe what I found…
dialogue.offer: Holy hell, the crash you recovered the black box from wasn't as old as I thought.  Check this out, it was on its approach to pick up a team sent to secure and destroy something called a 'Hazardous Waste Sarcophagus' in the middle of nowhere.  If the bird never picked up the team then we may still have a chance to meet up with them.  It includes an access code for the elevator and an encoded message for the team leader, I guess.  If we want to join up with what remains of the government then now may be our only chance.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck ya, America!
dialogue.rejected: Are you going to forfeit your duty when the country needs you the most?
dialogue.advice: If there is a military team down there then we better go in prepared if we want to impress them.  Carry as much ammo as you can and prepare to ditch this place if they have a second bird coming to pick them up.
dialogue.inquire: Having any trouble following the map?  Remember to search underground.
dialogue.success: Maybe these things are what remains of the team we were searching for…
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I out'ta whip your ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, we were so close.

dialogue.offer: I have asthma.  I need you to get an inhaler for me…
dialogue.accepted: Thank you!  This attack is really bad… I'm not sure how long I can live… like this…
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Please, <ill_die> without… your help!
dialogue.advice: Make sure it still has… some charges left…
dialogue.success: Alright, as long as I have one of these, I should be fine.
dialogue.success_lie: You're lying… I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: How am I not dead already?!

dialogue.offer: I have an infected wound.  I need you to get some antibiotics for me…
dialogue.accepted: Oh, thank you, thank you so much!  I probably don't have long, so hurry…
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Please, <ill_die> without your help!
dialogue.advice: Maybe check a pharmacy, behind the counter, or there might be some in somebody's bathroom.
dialogue.success: Yes!  I'll be right as rain in no time.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: How am I not dead already?!

dialogue.describe: We've got the flag, now we need to locate US forces.
dialogue.offer: We have the flag but now we need to locate US troops to see what we can do to help.  I haven't seen any but I'm figurin' one of those choppers that were flyin' round during th' outbreak would have a good idea.  If you can get me a black box from one of the wrecks I'll look into where we might open 'er at.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck yeah, America!
dialogue.rejected: Do you have any better ideas?
dialogue.advice: Survivors were talkin' 'bout seeing 'em falling out of the sky but I don't know where.  If I were a pilot I'd avoid crash landing in a city or forest though.  Black boxes are housed in the tail to survive the crash so check there when you do find one.  Now get to it!
dialogue.success: America, fuck yeah!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I oughta whip your ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, I'll have to find 'er myself.

dialogue.describe: With the black box in hand, we need to find a lab.
dialogue.offer: Thanks to your searching we've got the black box but now we need to have a look inside her.  Now, most buildings don't have power anymore but there are a few that might be of use.  Have you ever seen one of those science labs that have popped up in the middle of nowhere?  Them suckers have a glowing terminal out front so I know they have power somewhere inside 'em.  If you can get inside and find a computer lab that still works you ought to be able to find out what's in the black box.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck yeah, America!
dialogue.rejected: Do you have any better ideas?
dialogue.advice: When I was playin' with the terminal for the one I ran into it kept asking for an ID card.  Finding one would be the first order of business.
dialogue.success: America, fuck yeah!  I was in the guard a few years back so I'm confident I can make heads-or-tails of these transmissions.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I oughta whip your ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, I maybe we can find an egg-head to crack the terminal.

dialogue.offer: I hope you will find use from what you got out of the deposit box but I also have another job for you that might lead you to an opportunity to deal out justice for those who cannot.  First things first, we can't just look like ruffians.  Find us a deputy badge, easy enough?
dialogue.accepted: I'd check the police station.
dialogue.rejected: We're also official… just hang in there and I'll show you what we can really do.
dialogue.advice: They shouldn't be that hard to find… should they?
dialogue.success: Great work, Deputy.  We're in business.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the criminals if it hasn't already.

dialogue.describe: Does our flag still yet wave?
dialogue.offer: Does our flag still yet wave?  We're battered but not yet out of the fight, we need the old colors!
dialogue.accepted: Hell ya!  Find me one of those big ol' American flags.
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  God damned commie…
dialogue.advice: Find a large federal building or school, they must have one.
dialogue.success: America, fuck ya!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: You give up?  This country fell apart because no one could find a good man to rely on… might as well give up, I guess.

dialogue.offer: Our world fell apart because our leaders were as crooked as the con-men that paid for their elections.  Just find me one of those corporate accounting books and I'll show you and the rest of the world just who is at fault.
dialogue.accepted: You'll see, I know I'm right.
dialogue.rejected: I know it isn't pressing but the big corporations didn't get a chance to destroy the evidence yet.
dialogue.advice: Try a big corporate building of some sort, they're bound to have an accounting department.
dialogue.success: Great, let's see… uh… hmmm….  Fine, I didn't even do my own taxes but I'm sure this will prove their guilt if we get an expert to examine it.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the corporations if it hasn't already.

dialogue.describe: I hope I don't see many names I know…
dialogue.offer: I've lost so many friends… please find me a patient list from the regional hospital or doctor's office.  I just want to know who might still be out there.
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, I suppose it won't change what has already happened but it will bring me closure.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I just want to know what happened to everyone.
dialogue.advice: I bet you'll run into a lot of those things in the hospital, please be careful.
dialogue.success: Oh dear, I thought Timmy would have made it…
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: I bet some of them are still out there…

dialogue.describe: I wonder if a retreat might exist…
dialogue.offer: Everyone who dies gets back up, right?  Which means that whatever is causing this it must be airborne to have infected everyone.  I believe that if that is the case then there should be regions that were not downwind from where-ever the disease was released.  We need to find a record of all the weather patterns leading up to the outbreak.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks so much, you may save both of us yet.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, it was a long shot I admit.
dialogue.advice: I'm not sure, maybe a news station would have what we are looking for?
dialogue.success: These look more complicated than I thought, just give me some time.
dialogue.success_lie: This isn't what we need.
dialogue.failure: If only we could find a great valley or something.

dialogue.describe: Any variant is fine, I am not that choosy…
dialogue.offer: The sky has torn apart and creatures beyond our wildest imaginations lurk in the dark now.  I beg you, find me a holy symbol.  Maybe some faith can help me sleep better at night.
dialogue.accepted: May whatever god or spirits that now reign the world protect you.
dialogue.rejected: I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: A church must be full of them and who knows, maybe some of those <zombies> carry some.  But please, do not waste your time making one yourself.
dialogue.inquire: Any luck?  Please find me a holy symbol.  Any of them will do.
dialogue.success: Thank the heavens.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do me?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.description: Find a relic of a forgotten saint.  Places like <color_yellow>cathedrals</color> or <color_yellow>museums</color> might have one.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: As the world seems to abandon the reality that we once knew, it becomes plausible that the old superstitions that were cast aside may have had some truth to them.  Please go and find me a religious relic… I doubt it will be of much use but I've got to hope in something.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: I suppose a large church or cathedral may have something.
dialogue.inquire: Any luck?  Please find me a small relic.  Any relic will do.
dialogue.success: Thank you, I need some time alone now…
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: Now I don't mean to upset you but I'm not sure what I can do with the accounting ledger at the moment.  We do have a new lead though, the ledger has a safe deposit box under the regional manager's name.  Guess what, dumb sucker wrote down his combination.  Come with me to retrieve the box and you can keep any of the goodies in it that I can't use to press charges against these bastards.
dialogue.accepted: You may make a tidy profit from this.
dialogue.rejected: I know it isn't pressing but the world is going to be just as corrupt when we start rebuilding unless we take measure to stop those who seek to rule over us.
dialogue.advice: This shouldn't be hard unless we run into a horde.
dialogue.success: Great, anything I can't use to prosecute the bastards is yours, as promised.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the corporations if it hasn't already.

data.description: Retrieve the software in their computer marked on your map.

dialogue.describe: Oh man, I can't believe I forgot to download it…
dialogue.offer: There's some important software on my computer that I need on USB.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks!  Just pull the data onto this USB drive and bring it to me.
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  It's an easy job…
dialogue.advice: Take this USB drive.  Use the console, and download the software.
dialogue.inquire: So, do you have my software yet?
dialogue.success: Excellent, thank you!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: Wow, you failed?  All that work, down the drain…

dialogue.describe: It could be very informative to perform an analysis of zombie blood…
dialogue.offer: I need someone to get a sample of zombie blood, take it to a hospital, and perform a centrifuge analysis of it.
dialogue.accepted: Excellent.  Take this blood draw kit; once you've produced a zombie corpse, use it to extract blood from the body, then take it to a hospital for analysis.  After all that, bring the phlebotomy data back to me.
dialogue.rejected: Are you sure?  The scientific value of that blood data could be priceless…
dialogue.advice: The centrifuge is a bit technical; you might want to study up on the usage of computers before completing that part.
dialogue.inquire: Well, do you have the data yet?
dialogue.success: Nicely done.  I've copied the data over, talk to me again when I've had some time to look at it.
dialogue.success_lie: Wait, you couldn't possibly have the data!  Liar!
dialogue.failure: What a shame, that data could have proved invaluable…

data.description: Investigate the strange cabin in the woods and find an item that may clue you in about <color_yellow>a potential human sacrifice</color> the cult has performed, such as <color_yellow>human bones or other remains</color>.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: You have no idea how interesting this diary is.  I have two very promising leads… first things first, the Catholic Church has been performing its own investigations into global cult phenomenon and it appears to have become very interested in a local cult as of recently.  Could you investigate a location for me?  I'm not sure what was going on here but the priest seemed fairly worried about it.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path… You may need it this time more than the past excursions you have gone on.  There is a note about potential human sacrifice in the days immediately before and after the outbreak.  The name of the cult is believed to be the Church of Starry Wisdom but it is noted that accounts differ.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: I doubt the site is still occupied but I'd carry a firearm at least… I'm not sure what you might be looking for but I'm positive you'll find something out of the ordinary if you look long enough.
dialogue.inquire: I'm positive there is something there… there has to be, any luck?
dialogue.success: Thank you, your account of these… demonic creations proves the fears the churches had were well founded.  Our priority should be routing out any survivors of this cult… I don't known if they are responsible for the outbreak but they certainly know more about it than I do.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: I have another task if you are feeling up to it.  There is a prisoner that the priest made special mention of.  I was wondering if you could see what may have happened to him or if he left anything in his cell.  The priest admits the individual is rather unstable, to put it lightly, but the priest personally believed the man was some kind of repentant visionary.  I'm not in a position to cast out the account just yet… it seems the man has prophesied events accurately before concerning the Church of Starry Wisdom.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path… I can only imagine that the prison will be a little slice of hell.  I'm not sure what they would have decided to do with the inmates when they knew death was almost certain.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: The worst case scenario will probably be that the prisoners have escaped their cells and turned the building into their own little fortress.  Best case, the building went into lock-down and secured the prisoners in their cells.  Either way, navigating the building will pose its own difficulties.
dialogue.success: Thank you, I'm not sure what to make of this but I'll ponder your account.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: Well damn, you must be the guys here to pick me up…
dialogue.offer: I got the brief so I know what I'm getting into.  Let me be upfront, treat me like shit and I'm going to cover my own hide.  However, you treat me well and give me something to believe in, even if it's just a shiny bit of metal, and I'll do you right.  Without a strong band a man doesn't stand a chance in this world.  You ready to take charge boss?  This world could use a Sheriff just about now.
dialogue.accepted: Before we get into a major fight just make sure we have the gear we need, boss.
dialogue.rejected: I don't think you're going to find many other survivors who haven't taken up a faction yet.
dialogue.advice: I'm a pretty good shot with a rifle or pistol.
dialogue.success: Wait… are you really making me a deputy?
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think so…
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: You seem to know this new world better than most…
dialogue.offer: You're kitted out better than most… would you be interested in making this world a little better for the rest of us?  The towns have enough supplies for us survivors to start securing a foothold but we don't have anyone with the skills and equipment to thin the masses of undead.  I'll lend you a hand to the best of my ability but you really showed promise taking out that other beast.  You, I, and a 100 zombies laid to rest, what do you say?
dialogue.accepted: Hell ya, we may get ourselves killed but we'll be among the first legends of the apocalypse.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either… but then I remember that most of us survivors won't make it unless someone decides to take the initiative.
dialogue.advice: I'd secure an ammo cache and try to sweep a town in multiple passes.
dialogue.success: Man… you're a goddamn machine.  It was a pleasure working with you.  You know, you may just change our little neck of the world if you keep this up.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think that was quite a hundred dead zeds.
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: I've heard some bad rumors so I hope you are up for another challenge…
dialogue.offer: Apparently one of the other survivors picked up on an unusually dense horde of undead moving into the area.  At the center of this throng there was a 'leader' of some sort.  The short of it is, kill the son of a bitch.  We don't know what it is capable of or why it is surrounded by other zombies but this thing reeks of trouble.  Do whatever it takes but we can't risk it getting away.
dialogue.accepted: I'll lend you a hand but I'd try and recruit another gunslinger if you can.
dialogue.rejected: What's the use of walking away, they'll track you down eventually.
dialogue.advice: Don't risk torching the building it may be hiding in if it has a basement.  The sucker may still be alive under the rubble and ash.
dialogue.success: May that bastard never get up again.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think we got it yet.
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: The eater of the dead… something was ripping zombies to shreds and only leaving a few scattered limbs…
dialogue.offer: A few days ago another survivor and I were trying to avoid the cities by staying in the woods during the day and foraging for gear at night.  It worked well against the normal zeds but one night something caught onto our trail and chased us for ten minutes or so until we decided to split up and meet-up back here.  My buddy never showed up and I don't have the means to kill whatever it was.  Can you lend a hand?
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, make sure you're ready for whatever the beast is.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either.
dialogue.advice: I'd carry a shotgun at least, it sounded pretty big.
dialogue.success: You look a little shaken up, I can't tell you how glad I am that you killed it though.
dialogue.success_lie: Something in the shadows still seems to stare at me when I look at the woods.
dialogue.failure: I'm glad you came back alive… I wasn't sure if I had sent you to your death.

dialogue.describe: Oh god, I can't believe it happened…
dialogue.offer: My mom… she's… she was killed, but then she just got back up… she's one of those things now.  Can you put her out of her misery for me?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you… she would've wanted it this way.
dialogue.rejected: Please reconsider, I know she's suffering…
dialogue.advice: Find a gun if you can, make it quick…
dialogue.inquire: Well…?  Did you… finish things for my mom?
dialogue.success: Thank you.  I couldn't rest until I knew that was finished.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: Really… that's too bad.

dialogue.describe: I just need a place to start over…
dialogue.offer: I've accepted that everyone I used to know is dead… one way or another.  I really wish I could have done something to save my brother but he was one of the first to go.  I'd like to start over, just rebuild at one of the farms in the countryside.  Can you help me secure one?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, let's find a remote one so we don't have to worry about many zombies.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I just don't know what to do otherwise.
dialogue.advice: Traveling the backroads would be a good way to search for one.
dialogue.inquire: Shall we keep looking for a farm house?
dialogue.success: Well, my adventuring days are over.  I can't thank you enough.  Trying to make this place self sustaining will take some work but the future is looking brighter.  At least it ought to be safe for now.  You'll always be welcome here.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: I guess it was just a pipe dream.

dialogue.describe: Maybe they escaped to one of the camps…
dialogue.offer: I can't thank you enough for bringing me the patient records but I do have another request.  You seem to know your way around… could you take me to one of the FEMA camps?  I know some were overrun but I don't want to believe all of them could have fallen.
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, just bring me to the camp… I just want to see.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I don't know what else to do.
dialogue.advice: We should go at night, if it is overrun then we can quickly make our escape.
dialogue.inquire: Any leads on where a camp might be?
dialogue.success: I guess this wasn't as bright an idea as I thought.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying… I guess.
dialogue.failure: I bet some of them are still out there…

data.description: Find something that may reveal what the church's stance is on these events.  Something like <color_yellow>a priest's diary</color> would suffice.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: From what I understand, the creatures you encountered surrounding this relic were unlike anything I've heard of.  It is laughable that I now consider the living dead to be part of our ordinary reality.  Never-the-less, the church must have some explanation for these events.  I have located the residence of a local clergy man, could you go to this address and recover any items that may reveal what the church's stance is on these events?
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: If the information is confidential the priest must have it hidden within his own home.
dialogue.success: Thank you, a diary is exactly what I was looking for.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.description: Go to the cabin in the woods where the Tracker is camping and <color_yellow>recruit them</color>.

dialogue.describe: You seem to know this new world better than most…
dialogue.offer: We've got another problem to deal with but I don't think we can handle it on our own.  So, I sent word out and found us a volunteer… of sorts.  He's vain as hell but has a little skill with firearms.  He was supposed to collect whatever he had of value and is going to meet us at a cabin in the woods.  Wasn't sure how long we were going to be so I told him to just camp there until we picked him up.
dialogue.accepted: Roger, if he's a no-show then any other gunslinger will do… but I doubt he'll quit before we even begin.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either… but then I remember that most of us survivors won't make it unless someone decides to take the initiative.
dialogue.advice: I hope the bastard is packing heat… else we'll need to grab him a gun before we hit our next target.
dialogue.success: Great, just let me know when you are ready to wade knee-deep in an ocean of blood.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think so…
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.offer: I left my poor dog in a house, not far from here.  Can you retrieve it?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you!  Please hurry back!
dialogue.rejected: Please, think of my poor little puppy!
dialogue.advice: Take my dog whistle; if the dog starts running off, blow it and he'll return to your side.
dialogue.inquire: Have you found my dog yet?
dialogue.success: Thank you so much for finding him!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: Oh no!  My poor puppy…

name.str: Break into armory to retrieve family photo

dialogue.describe: I need you to get my family photo from the armory safe.
dialogue.offer: I left the only photo I have from my family in the armory.  I don't have the code, can you get in?
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, it's great to see someone willing to help a out.
dialogue.rejected: Well, I'll find someone else to do it for me, real shame with all those guns locked up too…
dialogue.advice: You look like a resourceful sort, maybe you can hack it or something.
dialogue.inquire: Got the photo?  Should've been in my gun safe.
dialogue.success: Thanks!  I'll be sure to put in a good word for you around town.
dialogue.success_lie: OK, then hand it over.
dialogue.failure: Shit happens.

data.description: Prove you're a survivor by surviving for 10 days after the Cataclysm, and then returning to the person who gave you this mission.

dialogue.describe: It's hard to tell who actually has the skills to survive these days…
dialogue.offer: It's hard surviving out here on our own, and we'd probably have a better chance working together.  Problem is, I don't really know you and what you're capable of.  You might have what it takes, or you might not.  Either way, I'm going to need some proof.  Come back in a few days and I'll gladly follow you.  It's basically a win-win for me: either you come back and I'll know you've got what it takes, or you don't and I'll know that I was right not to follow you.
dialogue.accepted: I'll see you then… or I won't, and then I'll know I made the right decision.
dialogue.rejected: Yeah, it was a long shot I admit.
dialogue.advice: Don't die.  If you're asking me for advice, that doesn't bode well for you.
dialogue.success: I'll be honest, I wasn't really expecting to see you again.  A promise is a promise, I'll follow you now!
dialogue.success_lie: I know time is relative and all that.
dialogue.failure: I'm not quite sure how you failed to survive AND are talking to me.

data.//: Unfailable condition used here just to make it work.

dialogue.offer: We should travel together.
dialogue.accepted: We can keep each other safe.
dialogue.rejected: Ugh, forget it then, I'll figure something out on my own.
dialogue.advice: It's crazy out there, nobody's going to make it on their own.
dialogue.success: Great!  I'm with you.
dialogue.success_lie: Wait, were you being sarcastic?
dialogue.failure: Ugh, forget it then, I'll figure something out on my own.

name.str: Gather cattail stalks to create cattail jelly

data.description: Gather <color_light_blue>20 cattail stalks</color> from the swamp and bring them back to <color_light_red>learn how to craft cattail jelly</color>.  Raise your <color_light_blue>ecology skill to at least 1</color> by harvesting cattail stalks or foraging in underbrush.

effect.u_message: You learn how to craft cattail jelly.

dialogue.describe: Medical services are a little sparse following <the_cataclysm>, but people have been surviving using their wits and the bounty of Mother Nature for a long time.  Care to learn a little?
dialogue.offer: Did you know that cattails are a source of a jelly that works as an antiseptic and analgesic?  Something like that is likely to be mighty helpful out here.  I want you to head to the nearest swamp, collect 20 cattail stalks, and bring them back here.  In exchange, I'll show you how to harvest the jelly, provided you can demonstrate you have the skills.
dialogue.accepted: Great!  Be careful out there, and don't be afraid to forage around in any underbrush you pass, too.  You never know what you'll find.
dialogue.rejected: Your loss.
dialogue.advice: The cattails grow in the fresh water in swamps.  You can't miss them.
dialogue.success: Great!  Hand them over and I'll show you how this works.
dialogue.success_lie: OK, then hand them over.
dialogue.failure: Well, that's a shame.
